I opened the Greek and it was steaming hot with gooey cheese, black olives, and banana pepper. I added lettuce for more depth. The flavors were mild, but tasty. Nothing that really wowed me or that I could not make at home.  I ate half and took the rest home. 
The New Orleans style was made with blackened chicken, red pepper and bacon nestled in melted cheese (of which he could not recall). He said he liked it. That was all. He fussed more over the cookie than he did over the Quesadilla. The cookies looked amazingly tasty. 

We agreed that, while this place was okay, it would not make our list of frequented establishments.

Avoid! Great location with dynamic view of Jackson Square, but it has nothing else going for it. Lackluster food and service; no locals would ever eat here, for it is known as just a tourist rip-off. Pay attention to your bill, as they sneak in an obligatory 15% "service" charge.
Cute Japanese restaurant in Old City. Fresh sushi and amazing ramen. Wonderful customer service! This is my new favorite go to for sushi and ramen. There is a great selection on the menu.

This is the second time experiencing In Riva, but the first review. 

Went twice on one night so I was able to experience two aspects of the place. The first time was pre-game for an event we had at the Laurel Hill Cemetery. We stood at the bar. The bar itself is very small and I felt like I was crowding the people sitting at the high top table behind me. The bartender was very nice but could have used more knowledge of the beer selection. They didn't seem to know much about the style of the beer. 

The second time was after the event. We were running late and I called to let them know (we had reservations at 9) and they were very pleasant and accommodating. When we arrived we sat at a table. One of the first things you notice is the pizza oven with Pizza's constantly going in and out of it. So we had to order pizza and really it's the only thing I've ordered and all I can say is fantastic.  We split two pizza's and took the rest home. We got the Marcherita pizza with white anchovy. The anchovies weren't your typical little salty fish, no, they were large semi-salty fish and the pizza was delicious. The other pizza,which we liked alittle better was the Mushroom and Zucchini, really great mushroom taste. The waitress was very friendly and we enjoyed having her as our server, but again could use more knowledge of the bar.

45 minutes later and I am still sitting here listening to that incessant music that pauses every once in a while to instruct me to unplug my cable box if I am having trouble with my cable. As soon as a representative comes on she asks me if I have unplugged my box. I told her I had been told 50 times to do so while I waited 45 minutes for her to answer my call....so I would be a real moron if I hadn't tried that by now. Let's not forget the appointments they set up for you that they don't bother keeping. No, I don't mind wasting 3 hours of work to wait for a tech who doesn't show. Thanks for the 20 bucks but you cost me more then that. But...my favorite of all time is the tech who sits in front of your house for 20 minutes without coming to your door. Then you call them and the techs notes say customer not home. "Let's set up another appointment". Comcast, get your shit together. You are like a billion dollar company and have the worst customer service. You are truly hated by most. Congrats!

There was a time I would have given Tryst 5 stars. Food was good, drinks reasonably priced and the house music best in town. During a recent visit July 7th the shift manager and wait staff had such the attitude - I found them to be pompus, arrogant and outright repugnant. The menu has erroded over the years from interesting to "safe". I guess the owner has lost his european flair and this now "just another place". Save your money and go the  champaign bar next door. Interesting food, great wine and champaign selection, attentive service and you can still enjoy the music from Tryst - its only 20 ft away.

Ft Worth Ribeye was perfect!!  Can't ask for a better meal and service for under $20!!!  Worth the drive from downtown St Pete.  Roasted nuts are addicting...hide them until they deliver your food.  Sat at the bar and was well attended even though I just had coffee and water.  From door to seat everyone goes out of the way to make your visit special.

The shop is cute and everything is displayed beautifully.  There is no lot nearby so parking may be weird but it's worth having to walk a few blocks in my opinion.  The items were all gorgeous, no sloppy frosting or whatever else here, you can tell the bakers really care about their work.

I found the prices a tad high to be honest but having gone through  most of my haul, the quality is top notch and is definitely worth the splurge every now and again. Between me and my parents were got a little of everything and I really recommend the red velvet cake (the best cake i've ever had seriously) and the various bars (key lime and lemon are not to be missed!). 

My major complaint was nothing had prices on it, so you had to ask constantly and when I went it was very busy so that quickly became a hassle.  Also, the women at the counter seemed to be a bit overwhelmed by the crowd so things didn't run as smoothly as they should have (it was early afternoon on a weekday...still busy but i'm sure Saturday or sunday mornings are worse). Maybe management should look into getting some extra help! 

I did want to shout out to the women at the counter though, someone came in to pick up a special order cake for the kentucky derby of all things and there was some very minor issue with it that the woman was very upset over (unneeded in my opinion- the issue had no effect on her ability to enjoy the cake it was purely aesthetic and truly a small detail) and the woman helping her was very kind and understanding and considerate when dealing with this drama queen.

My family and I was on a quick getaway trip and decided to eat here. Not only was the food excellent, it was within walking distance from my hotel! 
Loved it!!

Vacationed in New Orleans for Halloween. Mr. B's was recommended by all the locals. It is probably one of the best restaurants I have been to in all my travels. We tried almost everything on the menu from shrimp, to crab cakes, to salad, to bread pudding.... everything was AMAZING!  But if you're going to just try one thing... the BBQ shrimp is the best hands down.

If you want atmosphere, go somewhere else.

I had dinner there other night for the first time, after having lived across the street from them for over a year. Their crab soup is *Simply Amazing*.

I honestly loved my fajita platters both times I've come here, but the rest of the food was meh, and the service is the absolute WORST. Like it literally makes me want to tear my hair out its so bad. The first time we waited over an hour for our food, never mind that the restaurant was just about empty. The second time, I came with my parents and they were miserable because despite the fact that the restaurant was again--empty, we waited 20 minutes for a table, then once seated, my mom had to literally stand up to flag someone down, that someone happened to be a manager who had to take our order, because our waitress didn't decide to show up until we had been sitting there for 30 minutes! Then once the manager took our drinks order, it took 20 minutes for it to come. FINALLY!! An hour and 10 minutes later, our food showed up. My brother's burrito was scarfed down in about 4 minutes, and he was left hungry and unsatisfied at the quality of it. I loved my fajita platter but felt bad for everybody else. Seriously mad mex needs to figure their service issues out, or close down bc coming here isn't worth your sanity or frustration.

Second time's the charm. Stopped by once to have a duplicate key made only to find that their hours were not at my convenience. My bad I guess. Stopped by a second time a week or so later - (it's close to home, so why now swing by?) - this time they were open and they proved to be very helpful.

Pleasant encounter with the gentleman behind the counter who quickly cut several odd-shaped keys for me that the big box stores could not duplicate.

Quick, polite, efficient, and cost-effective.

Wow!  We had the most amazing food and service at Blue Fig!  The food is all freshly made.  We had the hummus and home made chips to start...highly recommend!!! They have a variety of gluten and dairy free options that are delicious. The falafel salad was the best. 
      Great to find a restaurant close by that's both healthy and affordable.

What to get: beignets
Service: 4/5
Atmosphere: cafe, fast take out
Wait: 5 mins (Saturday 10AM for 2)
Parking: large parking lot

The Experience: [July 2016]
I'm no stranger to Cafe Du Monde's beignets in the French quarter, so I'm okay trying other locations further from the original. This one is located inside a mall, so it's relatively spacious and easy to get to. There's a huge parking lot encircling the mall, so no worries there either.

The Cafe Du Monde here is reminiscent of a mall food court level place. It's a quick service type where you order at the counter and you find your seat to enjoy your beignets and coffee at one of the few tables.

If you've never had a beignet, you're in for a treat. It's like a lighter doughnut with a mountain of powder sugar on top. Very messy, you'll need a pile of napkins to clean up afterwards. Eat them while they're fresh and hot! In comparison with the ones in the French Quarter, the quality is about the same.

So if you're looking for the infamous Cafe Du Monde beignet, you can try it at further locations. Less traffic, less tourists, faster service. Just the location isn't anywhere scenic, but it's part of the tradeoff.

Everything about this place is huge!  It's a Vegas-style hotel minus the casino.  Restaurants, entertainment--even an indoor gondola ride!

We really didn't stay in the hotel much though and it probably would have been more convenient to stay downtown.  Opryland is a good 10 minute drive away. They do offer a shuttle to downtown that will pick you back up until 1:30am from the Wildhorse Saloon for $15 per person.

Overall our room was really nice, we ordered room service once and it was okay.  There were several proms happening the weekend we stayed here, so that was kind of neat to see all of the kids dressed up and fancy.

If you're looking to stay out late in the bars, then I would stay downtown and avoid driving.

Huge fan, especially since it is right by our apartment. I've always had speedy and friendly  service here. The main allure has to be the breakfast dishes, which I believe I've had in all but one instance, but the burrito on the other visit did the trick too. Get the chilaquiles! Or a skillet or an omelet. Yes, it gets crowded. Maybe they should expand?
A beautiful space that sometimes offers unique experiences. I went to see a screening of Casablanca where the orchestra performed the soundtrack live! It was incredible.
I prefer this Felix's over the French quarter. Much better food here than Brisbi's - they need a drink list. Excellent food & fun on the lakefront!

This is a hidden gem! This is my first review but I had to give it 5 stars for the amazing crepes at a good price! I also had a delicious caramel milkshake. The crepes here are cheaper than the market and they don't come in a cone. When I come back to New Orleans I'll be coming here :) my mum and I really enjoyed it.

Best Italian in St. Louis for my money!  Visited for the first time over the weekend with my wife, son and parents-in-law.  The food is great but the service is incredible.

I can't speak enough about the service.  Every staff member was incredibly friendly, pleasant, professional and seemed to genuinely enjoy their jobs.  We brought my two-year-old son based on some reviews on Yelp that said it was a restaurant for all ages.  They were very accommodating.  They had a high chair waiting for us and provided him some crayons.

We ordered the toasted ravs for an appetizer.  These rank up there with some of the best I've had.  I ordered the spinach and prosciutto pizza.  My wife had the cannolli.  The PILs ordered the Straw and Hay and the Chocolate Fettuccine and a house salad.

Everyone raved about their food.  Naturally, as an Italian restaurant, they gave us more food than we could eat.  Another nice touch was the dinner rolls with hummus rather than the traditional olive oil or butter.

I love this place and probably can't eat Italian food anywhere else in town.
Excellent food. Very authentic taste. By far the best Mexican food I've ever had. Not the greatest "curb appeal" but worth the effort to find.

Food was ok. Our bartender was a sweetheart but I was a little taken back by the fact that the owner or MOD came down during our meal to reprimand her for changing the music that was playing. Extremely unprofessional and tacky to yell at employees in front of customers. Other than that, it's just a hole in the wall with mediocre, quick food. Not the worst place, just don't request to change the music.

I can't even tell you how much I love Delicia. I've been a number of times now, and each visit has been superb. Their food is always to die for, whether it's the vegetarian potato tacos or the empanadas. They also have the best margarita I've had in Indianapolis yet. Service was also A+. What more could you ask for?

Ordered Chicken vindaloo and chicken rice biryani with naan bread. First off let me say the portions for the biryani is massive and definitely worth the price. Nicely seasoned basamati rice and very aromatic. The vindaloo was decent

I was looking for momji ramen. (it use to be that area)

I couldn't find it, but I saw this place and thought I would try it.
it wasn't bad, I think reno has sooo many sushi places that you should try and find out which one you like best.  I can think of at least 4 other sushi places that I like better than here.

The service was really good but i don't think I'll come back here.

Great knowledgable service! The staff are passionate about their work and it shows. Be prepared to wait forever for anything. Took my dog in for "emergency care", they were knowledgeable but at 1am I don't need to know the nitty gritty and be explained in extreme detail that she should eat a bland diet.  The 4 stars (should be 5) are just for the loooooooooong wait and the loooooooooong explanation which could've been resolved in a standard 3 sentence note
Cute little place, nice atmosphere. I ordered a grilled pork vermicelli and the noodles were cold, no brownie points there. The pork and flavor were on point though. Overall, I wasn't impressed.

A somewhat strange assortment of seating choices greet you at the door.
As you seem to walk right from the street to the dining area.   Staff is super friendly, service is quick and responsive.   The larger sushi platters looked more like art then dinner.   Pho was very good too.   We'll certainly return

This is the place!!If you need a good quality haircut in Nashville, go to Green Hills Barber Shop and ask for Sara. 

I went in yesterday for a cut and Sara did an awesome job. She asked me what kind of cut I wanted and I gave here some ideas, and she did the rest. The shop has a very traditional, but relaxed, feel to it.  

I have tried out a few other places in town and have never found anyone that did a well enough job to return. After the last person cut my hair was clueless on how to use clippers,I knew I needed to find somewhere better. Green Hills Barber Shop is that somewhere. This is the best cut that I have ever had. 

Both barbers really know what they are doing, and they are extremely nice and welcoming. If you are looking for a really great haircut in Nashville, Green Hills is your place!

Where is the best CrossFit Gym in the Indianapolis Area? Right here at CrossFit Zionsville! It is the most diverse, friendly, motivating, and family oriented CrissFit Gym in Indy! You will see results if you are consistent! Highly recommend this CrossFit Gym, two thumbs up!

Stromboli $7.95!!! Look at the size of this and with traditional NY style bread. For app we had homemade meatballs and sauce which were delicious. The ribeye steak was a nice cut of meat with a side of potatoes that were deliciously crunchy! We are definitely coming back to this place with great food that doesn't break the bank.

Been wanting to try this place for a while, but waited for it to be open a little bit to work out the kinks of a new restaurant.  Went right before the lunch rush on a Thursday.  Line was pretty short, and moved along pretty fast with plenty of open tables.   

They have an abundance of meats and sides and I ordered the brisket with an add-on of sausage and for sides collards, smoked jalapenos and fried pickles and it came with a biscuit.  All of it looked good but in the end it was meh since my entire entree was basically luke warm almost cold, which was surprising since I watched them take out a fresh brisket and I got the first slices but surprisingly it was not hot (not even warm).  The brisket, albeit room temp, was good.  The sausage wasn't anything special, but still good.  As for the sides: collards, good but nothing to get excited over.  They do use ham hock but it's missing some more salt and some of the vinegar tang to it.  The smoked jalapenos are stuffed with cheese and wrapped in bacon, which sounds amazing, but this is the type of side that needs to be fresh.  It def had a great taste and probably would be amazing if it had just come out of the oven.  The fried pickles had the potential to be amazing, they use thick cut round garlic pickles (my fav) but then they just put way too much breading on them that if you ate them with the breading you lost the taste of the pickle.  Finally, the biscuit.  It look good, it's a heavy dense kind (not light and flaky at all) and I commented on if it was hot that butter and honey would be amazing on it (but alas it was not hot and there was no butter to be found, though didn't see honey).  

So all in all, it was just okay.  It has the potential to be great, but with everything being luke warm and mostly bland it just turned me off.  There are other BBQ places around that are just as good so I'm not sure I'll be back.

Dangerous.  They are OK with life endangering, lazy repairs.  My wife insists on taking her Saturn there because they used to be a Saturn dealer.  She recently bought a new set of overpriced tires and these pitiful pukes did not put in new valve stems.  Down to about 13 psi by the time she got home.  The worst.  She took my truck there for a surprise gift oil change once which I really appreciated until SURPRISE, oil all over the garage due to finger tight plug.  Buffoons

The decor, service, and presentation are awesome! Makes you feel special and in a different country altogether. I had the lemon blueberry cake and macaroon cookies. Set me back close to $30.00. The cookies were delicious and the cake was light and sorry but lacked the flavors I would expect from lemon and blueberry mix. All in all I will definitely go back again!

Who knew Chalfont was privy to a hidden treasure! Amazing food, hip atmosphere, courteous staff. Alligator Roll = pure decadence with a flare of heat!!! Fills up quickly, reservations strongly encouraged. Awesome, awesome, awesome...worth a try!

Where do I even begin? My coworkers and I came across this place when we ventured out of our hotel one evening. It ended up being the only place we regularly went. The staff at this place are incredible. They always seem to have enough bartenders behind the bar and they know when it's going to be busy. Service is prompt. You can tell that the management has placed an emphasis on customer service. employees are very friendly, and outgoing. speaking of the management, I had the pleasure to meet the husband and wife that own this place. They are extremely pleasant and very fun to talk to. as for the smoke, yes as mentioned in previous reviews there is smoke inside the bar. You will however find that it's not the typical smoke you find in a rundown 80's dive bar with some cover band in the background. This place has adequate ventilation, and the smoke is not overpowering.  The patrons that frequent this establishment all seem to be very cordial , and are there to just have a good time. I highly recommend paddywagon to anybody in the area!

The Barbary, where do I begin?

Since moving to Philly in 2011, I feel I've been to the Barbary my fair share of times. Each time is another memory and something I probably wouldn't have experienced in say...Old City. When you really just want to go out and drink with your friends while listening to good music the Barbary is the place for you. You don't have to get dressed up to go to the Barbary, it's the BARBARY.

 A big part of going there is that you frequently find yourself surrounded by a mixture of people ranging from a hipster in an ironic Cosby sweater to what appears to be a nouveau-goth girl reminiscent of an extra from the movie The Craft. They have tons of different themed nights most notably Tigerbeats (indie) and Makeout Club/Through Being Cool (pop-punk) along with a plethora of other special nights. It's a fun place to go every once in awhile and sing your heart out, plus it's in walking distance of the Barcade and other fun places to explore. It's kind of hit or miss with the bartenders but that's to be expected anywhere, it's cash only so yeah, you should probably hit the ATM before you go. Just don't expect too much, have fun, and you'll be just fine.
Two takeout dishes, chicken tikka and palak lamb, both ordered extra spicy.  Lamb dish was very nice, but the chicken dish had zero spiciness.

Archway is an unassuming, if not a little scary looking sandwich joint underneath the parking garage on 8th street between Arch and Filbert.  This is NOT a place I would go to if I had not been taken there.  However, after 2 years working at 8th and Market it is my savior on a hungover morning.  This my friends is the home of the perfect bacon egg and cheese on a kaiser.  The perfect proportions of all three ingredients and the crispiest bacon....with a little hot sauce this sandwich rights all wrongs.  The staff knows there regulars and greets everyone with a "hey sweetie, what can I get for you today?" However, this question is mute because the grill guy, in my case already has my sandwich going since he got on it as soon as I walked in the door.  Apart from this I can also vouch for their Texas Tommys.  It's super inexpensive as well, the kind of place you feel well fed after having spent about 5 bucks.  Anyway, if you love Bacon Egg and cheese on a kaiser, I would seek this place out, if not, then it may not be worth the pilgrimage.

The lovely ladies of Rathbone Mansions get a five star rating.  We were here in early June, and we were pleasantly surprised.  I only say surprised, because of some of the previous reviews.  I completely agree with the previous reviewer who said if you want a Hilton, stay at a Hilton.  It's an old house. Our room was nice and comfortable.  The pool was a great afternoon respite.  It's so easy to walk to Frenchman Street and the French Quarter from here.  Over the weekend, we went to the Zydeco Festival in Louis Armstrong Park a short distance away, and Ms. Pat was so nice to offer up some lawn chairs for us to take.  We'll be staying here the next time we're in NOLA.
Decent food. Messed up take out order the one time I did order out with them. Bit pricey.

I am sort of a simple man, so I had never been to a liquor bar before. I have been to The Libertine twice and had a good experience both times. They use fresh ingredients all the way down to the crushed ice, which they crush with a mallet right at the bar. 

The biggest problem I ran into was figuring out which restroom was the men's. You have to look at the hair on the dimly lit pictures that indicate which is which, all the faces look the same.

This is always a favorite with our family, whether driving or grabbing hot chocolate and bundling the kiddos up and walking thru...the lights & houses are always fun and festive. 

Something our family looks forward to every year!

Going to Sam's is always an adventure. You never know just what he is going to feel like adding to that roll you just ordered.  Which is mainly the reason I am not so much of a fan. I can be picky... especially when it comes to sushi. That and the fact that I have yet to be allowed to order miso soup with my meal. But the prices here are good especially if you are a quantity over quality kind of person. Sam's does take credit cards but just be sure that you don't leave him a tip. Unless of course you like to see a grown Japanese sushi chef flip his lid.

The Tuscan Tower rooms have always been the best in town but it appears they are in need of some renovation.  On my last visit, the reading lamp in between the two beds was flat out missing, yep, just an empty pedestal (not a good look to the room).  Immediately notified the front desk.  Also, it appears they have removed many of the decorative pillows, etc. that make the room appear more luxurious, not sure why they aren't being replaced.  Overall, the room just looks tired. The casino looks dark and dated with terrible ventilation.  Plus, what's with the double security to use your comp dollars?  Please enter your PIN and show me your ID to get a latte? Then, stand in line at the passport club desk to show your ID yet again to get your free play?  Really??!!  Ridiculous.  Have a little class Peppermill, these are your customers. You get three stars for the Terrace Lounge and a nice swimming pool.

I went back to the Please-U-Restaurant when I was in New Orleans recently and once again they didn't disappoint! I had the pork chop for breakfast and it was perfectly seasoned! We spoke with the delightful waitress who was telling us about the places she lived in various parts of the country! This is my breakfast spot when I'm in NOLA!
It s cheap drinking and average bar food at best. The service is hit or miss but its still a great place to go to watch a sporting event. I normally stop in when getting my car serviced next door.
Perfect burger stop on our way home down the coast. Great family place with play areas for the kids.
Dr. Nancy Pruett has been my dentist for over 20 years! She and her staff are caring, kind and professional. I highly recommend Dr. Pruett for your dental care

This place was ok, it definitely didn't blow my mind. Well, the brussel sprout appetizer did blow my mind because it was fantastic. The entree, though, did not blow my mind. I went simple and got the burger, it wasn't cooked quite the way I ordered it. Additionally, I had removed a tomato slice from my burger because it wasn't quite ripe and I'm not a lover of tomatoes all the time. A waiter walked over and informed me that I could have asked for the burger without the tomato...uh, duh? I have been to restaurants before. I just wasn't hugely impressed. Our waiter was great, though, and super helpful.
Good south Indian food.  Great Hyderabadi Biriyani on the weekends.

Yummy. This is the best place to eat for this type of cuisine. Very small place but they seemed to fit us in in a reasonable amount of time. Generous portions ! Broken English but still understood us very well. Shrimp and vegetables is my favorite !!

I love the birthing center! We switched from my OB because I wanted to try giving birth without all the pressures if intervention (watch the movie the business of being born). My husband was not thrilled at first about it so we comprised that I would go there but have a hospital birth. Between the appointments with the midwives and the classes he totally changed his mind and was all about having our baby there. I'm so happy we did, the midwives were supportive and once my son was born he was able to just stay with me! Then when we wanted to go home we went home. So different then my friend's hospital experiences. I will say the answering service is not great for new patients, we had to just drop by over there to set an appointment. Once I was a patient the midwives on call would always call back to answer questions.
The chicken and the ribs entrees were overly-salty. I like my foods full of flavor, but not salt. But still it was pretty good, and the parking lot was convenient. The sides were good though.
This place is HORRIBLE.  1 cashier during winter break? Great planning management.... I have already been waiting in like for 25 MINUTES!!!

Everything I got was delicious! Needed to get some soup after a long night and decided to come here. The braised need noodle soup was delicious! I loved their noodles. We also got the tofu and calamari, both were great as well!

I was trying to find this place on yelp ao I can go back and now I found it. Someone brought me to this restaurant a while back & I have to say I truly enjoyed my meal. I probably ordered white sauce spaghetti with mussels. I can't exactly recall but I knew the food was great!! ;-) Sorry I occasionally I get food coma- you know, when the food is good and you ate a bit too much. Lol! Can't wait to stop by when I am in the area!

The slowest sonnets I have ever been to. At least 30 minutes in the drive through line. The order wasn't correct, and the employees weren't paying attention to what they were doing.  

With an exit with so many other options I would not recommend this Sonnys to anyone - unless of course you enjoy watching paint dry.

I really wanted bagel and lox but they were out of bagels so I opted for the lox eggs Benedict. It came out with the lox fried! Yuck! Since I won't send anything back unless it is inedible I lived with it. I just don't understand frying lox. Who does that?  Otherwise this is a good diner with attentive wait staff but I just can't get past the fried lox.  Lox, by definition, are not cooked but smoked only. If it is going to be fried, then it's just salmon.

I can usually count on prompt service and good food when I go to cpk. today, the host greeted us warmly, but my good experience ended there. it took over 30 min to get our pizza. the server brought 3small pieces of toast to hold us over. then, the pizza was over done. the basil was burnt. then, it took so long to get the check I had to leave while my husband stayed behind to pay. very disappointed in my latest experience

I had a great experience working with Chris Williams and Mike Ludrick in helping my parents find a new civic. As they are elderly I didn't want to shuttle them around from place to place or have them spend a lot of time dealing with marketing pitches. Conicelli Honda was the perfect place to start and end with, the team worked with me over the phone and was very professional, courteous, honest, no gimmicks. Once we quickly had figured things out I took my parents in and the car and paperwork were exactly as described, no surprises. We got a great deal and were very happy with the car and the experience. Simple and straightforward. Looking forward to working with them again, definitely recommended.

First of all, cash only. Which they prominently display, but if you're reading this and didn't catch that in the yelp description, you'd be missing out on delicious food. They have a decent menu of tacos, tortas etc. In addition they have a large variety of serve yourself condiments that are delicious and make the food that much better. It's outdoor seating but they have a tent so you are in the shade. I would recommend absolutely this as an affordable and delicious lunch option!

Loved it! The owner was really laid back and sweet, really great taste, excellent seamstress and not to pricy. Hands down best experience I've had. Would recommend her to all of my friends and family.

We were in the mood for some Malaysian food and stumbled upon Penang! We ordered the beef rendang and mango chicken. They were meh. Just ok. Nothing special. The beef rendang was so chewy and dry and the mango chicken  looks pretty on plate but it was way too saucy and oily! We couldn't finish it for that reason because we didn't want to end up reaching for bottles of water afterwards. Also  there were def more mango slices than chicken. Was totally not worth the $$ and def suggest to not order this!

High quality ingredients, fast and friendly service makes this an instant favorite of ours. Family friendly, pet area with picnic tables out back. Cool vibe, sports on TV, good beer on tap, and Kombucha on Tap? All this and the best part was still the quality tacos, sides and fresh hot chips out of the kitchen. I haven't had great food like this, creative and interesting since moving from Chicago.

Wouldn't go here again..... I got my belly button pierced...first off it was pierced crooked, secondly the artist was making really Inappropriate jokes the whole time... Not to mention the fact that he told me about one girl who he pierced who thought the pain was so bad she fainted...Like that's not something you should be talking to customers about as they are about to get their piercing.....NOT COOL! I also hated the fact that he bad mouthed other shops and tried saying that he was the best piercer ever because he's been doing it for this long and blah blah blah.... Sorry buddy but if you were the best my piercing wouldnt have been crooked...wouldn't recommend

Just experienced probably the greatest tacos that I've ever tasted. The cashier was wonderful and gave me her recommendations which I followed The fish taco was so fresh and so delicious and complemented by the sauces provided, I literally sat there in a state of amazement. My second taco was the Carnita. Usually braised pork loses its flavor. Here it not only maintained its flavor, it was picked by the spices and accompaniments. Also, the other sauce provided on the table just took this to unbelievable Heights. I highly, highly recommend this restaurant

I stumbled across this fantastic place while wandering down Magazine St. As Californian vegetarians, we were, to put it mildly, THRILLED! And then the food came and we were astounded. We opted for the tofu pesto sandwich - Delicious. Meat eaters are welcome here too though. I'd say its the perfect brunch spot. :-)

We have been bringing our rescue here for nearly a year and have nothing but great experiences.  Awesome, convenient, always able to fit us in during urgent situations.  Cautious and not overly eager to treat unnecessarily.   Would highly recommend.

I can't even explain how much fun I had at Picasso & Wine! Let me just tell you, I am artistically challenged to the point where I can't even draw a good stick figure. I was actually nervous about spending the money on a class knowing I haven't painted anything since elementary school. But I'm so glad my best friend talked me into going with her! Their calendar on their website had plenty of options to choose from; I was so indecisive! After much thought and consideration, I ended up choosing a sailboat painting. 

We were welcomed with a smile as we walked through the door. Our instructor had asked if we have ever been to a Picasso & Wine class & after finding out this was our first time, she showed us the ropes. She showed us to a couple of seats that were right up front and then pointed us in the direction of the bar for a complimentary drink. My first thought as I walked in the door was how amazing the atmosphere of this place is, it really lightens up the mood!

The class filled up quickly, nearly every seat in the room was taken. I was lucky to have gotten there early enough to grab a seat directly in front of our instructor. Don't worry though, even if you have to sit towards the back, there are plenty of screens around the entire room that shows live feed of what your instructor is doing. She was also using a headset piece that allowed everyone to be able to hear what she was saying. 

The instructor went step by step, in detail, while we painted the sailboat together as a group. I love how she asked multiple times if anyone was having trouble and needed some extra guidance, I thought it was very considerate of her. The class itself took around two hours or so with a small break in the middle for a refill on drinks & a restroom break. At the end of the class, the instructor took pictures of each individual group with their paintings on the mini stage. To my surprise, my painting looked awesome! It was one of those moments where I felt like I was a kid again and wanted to rush home to show my mom what I had painted. 

After the crowds were leaving, my bestfriend and I were one of the last people left. We had brought out empty glasses up to the bar where we met the owner. I wish I remembered her name! She was extremely sweet; we ended up conversing with her for over an hour after closing. I appreciate when an owner of a local business genuinely cares about the experience you've had. I will definitely be doing this again!

Coal on the verge of being diamond

If it hasn't been said, I'm going to say it, this will be the Chapterhouse of Queen Village.  Soon you'll have to wait for chairs or do the walkthrough to see if you can get a seat.  With three separate sections, a front room, a back study hall and a cozy patio, it offers the right space to any coffee dweller.    

Tea isn't my bag, but they host a huge selection for the area - tea lovers rejoice.  The coffee I ordered was excellent and they made it in a press for me, awesome.  I tried a carrot cake which was okay, I should have went with the green tea cupcake like others have mentioned.  

I think this shop is still fairly new, at least, I could smell the fresher paint and noticed a lack of city buildup grind on the floorboards.

I'll need a few more visits to really flesh out a good review but as it stands, this place is great.
The price was as advertised. The service was top notch and the room was better than expected. Located right next to Bourbon Street and the Absinthe house. I will definitely stay here again.

Ordered takeout for dinner - asked if they could put a rush on it and they did - food arrived when they said it would in 20 minutes! Great online ordering system. Food was delicious - will definitely order from there again.

WOW!  I come to town once every 4 months and always make sure to stop by here at least once a visit.  That smoked mackerel is just something you can't get anywhere else.  The frosted mug of root beer only makes it better.

Spa Aria is my favorite getaway in New Orleans.  The staff is very attentive and really want to provide you with the best experience possible.  I've had a variety of massage types and I've also taken advantage of treating myself to a last minute facial.  

I always try to make room for a visit when I'm in town!

I used to come here a lot while in Reno for business shortly after it opened, then my career took me to other places. We're here for a long weekend if relaxation & had to come back to Brew Bros for old time sakes. The IPA was very disappointing, it had minimal taste, seemed flat & just not good. Either they've tamed the recipe so beer minions that like tasteless stuff will be happy, or the lines are dirty & need to be cleaned. Thank goodness they have a good whiskey selection so the evening wasn't a loss.

Now to the food. We decided on appetizers instead of meals. The chicken wings were very small, but cooked "a little extra" as I asked & were really yummy. The Basalmic Brussels Sprouts were a total hit - I'd definitely order those little heads of vegetable heaven again. The Burnt Ends were meh & way too fatty. Overall, it was ok, nothing special, nothing too horrible.

Until we came back later after some gambling & drinking & needing something to soak up some booze. We ordered Garlic Parmesan Fries thinking they would be just what is needed. How disappointing the basket of out of the bag frozen fries were. Even Ore-Ida frozen fries (which are horrible) would have been better. The garlic & parmesan, what little there was, wouldn't even stick to the aweful undercooked & over-starchy excuse for fries. The bartender said they used to be awesome but management recently changed them & that every customer says they are no good now. I say they suck & should be taken off the menu.

Other than that, it was a solid 2 1/2  experience.

Wonderful! That's the best description of this cool little spot that I stopped into for Sunday brunch.  I stopped in when it was nearly empty which was great for me because I had the chance to chit chat with the staff about football.  
But let's talk about the food!  I had the house omelette of spinach, bacon and fontina cheese, with a side of grits and toast.  They use the best quality stuff and you can taste it!  So yummy!  Service was fast, super friendly, and on point.  
If you are in Dunedin, you need to take the time to stop into this great cafe for a meal. You won't be disappointed!

The name gives a clear picture of the type of food you'll have: yummy, rich, tender, and after you eat it, you'll feel very drowsy. I think I have taken or have tried to take a nap every single time after I got home from this place.
 
There is a lot to choose from on the menu (almost too much).  

The wait to get seated can be horrible on weekends, but once you're in, the place works like clockwork. The staff is friendly, isn't impatient, and gets you everything you want fast.

No less than five people, from the busboy to the owner behind the counter, wished us a friendly 'goodnight' on our way out. That NEVER happens! 
Great Italian classic meals at good prices. 
Not fancy. (There is a small TV in the dining room) but caters to families with children, small parties and everything in between. Not a quiet, romantic meal, but a tasty one.
Store is marked closed but it is still open. They still have alot to sell. Prices are pretty good. Good percentage off. I will miss this store at this location.
Been coming here forever!  They are the best!  Yummy salad bar and pizza as well as other Italian dishes.  Busy but friendly service.  Kathleen is the best server ever!  Can't wait to go back!

They are awesome! Great team of Physical therapists: professional, friendly, being going for  two months now due to the injuries caused by a car accident. I can't tell which therapist is better, because they are all simply AMAZING!

Delicious fresh chips and guacamole. I had the sopa with sausage, tostada with spicy chicken, and a burrito with carnitas. All were excellent. The only complaint is that the paper lining the plate ended up in my food.

Great Food, Organic & Gluten Free Options readily available. Casual Atmosphere that helps transport you to the Island of Hawaii - even if it is just for an Hour during Lunch. Friday night Hula shows are also a hit with Young & Old alike. The service is excellent, You can beat Free Hugs from Mama or the Owner, Teresa! ... I'm now craving popovers. mmmmmmmm

This is the worst Hertz location. I rent a car once or twice a week for work and have been to a lot of Hertz locations. The customer service is poor, the car pick up location is inconvenient and the cars never have a full tank of gas. Let me share with you some lessons learned, which the Hertz people should tell you but don't:

1. Before you leave the rental counter, make sure you have a parking ticket to exit the garage.
2. I have never rented a car from this location with a full tank of gas. They tell you it has a "little less than full". How the heck do you return a car "a little less than full"? I always end up filling up the tank for them because I don't know when to stop pumping. 
3. The cars used to be in the downstairs garage of 30th St station. Not anymore.  Go out the rental office and make a right, up the ramp until you find the escalator. Take escalator up. Walk across the overpass and take the escalators down. Leave the building and cross the walkway to the rental cars, which are outdoors. So, if it is raining or snowing, good luck.
4. Take parking ticket from lesson 1 to exit the parking area.
5. Upon return, just park in any spot and bring your keys back to the rental counter (back into the building, up the escalator, across the overpass, down the escalator, across the length of the station) to return the keys. Don't expect a verbal confirmation of your total, don't expect a smile or someone wishing you a good day. Just walk away vowing to take a cab the next time.

Ask for Phil...I have read some reviews that have called him a bit of a Chatty Kathy and it's true. However, the service he provides is stellar. His reccomendations are good...I enjoy the octopusm but last time it was a bit overdone. You can eat here cheaply if you want just a little something. I tend to spend about a hundred bucks for 2 people, but have a bottle of wine and desert, not to mention numerous tapas. Try it, you'll like it.

I gave 4 stars because it has no private space for parties. That is a big negative

Lobster Mac & Cheese is the ONLY reason it gets 2 stars.....service ALWAYS poor and depending who comes in before or after you, you can wait an eternity to be seated.  Not the place where EVERYONE is made to feel special.  Sad but true.

A decent coffeehouse with lots of seats & tables for working, but there's no WiFi, which makes it kind of a useless cafe if you want to do work. Both of the green teas sold here were very refreshing though.
Best wings I have found in Tucson. Never dined in, I always had take out. Always been great! Habanero wings are the best if you like heat. If not try the sweet Asian.

This is a great little place! Gyros, Greek salad with chicken, hummus and pita all delicious! At other places at times salads are lacking enough meat, but not here! Plenty of chicken and the salad is enough for two meals. I always leave with a box and have it for a second meal. The pitas are some of the best that I have had! They also do catering and have a television screen with pictures of all of the yummy platters they are able to do. Each time service has been friendly and welcoming. You can get your food to go or eat inside at one of the several tables.

Omg. The lumberjack!!! Yumm. We loved everything there:). Super friendly staff. Lots of fun variety pizzas. Loved the crust, local beers on tap was nice. Can't wait to go back.  Kids ate every bite without the usual normal complaints to urge them to finish. Military discount was a nice plus.

This review is for the restaurant and hotel together. Restaurant alone would get 5, hotel 3. First, the hotel. My girlfriend and I arrived by bike, and our host seemed a bit unwelcoming. We had read some not positive reviews about the hospitality there, so were prepared for a negative experience. Upon further experience though, we realized that our host is just an eccentric lady, and is actually super sweet. She met us in the parking lot to take our credit card so she could get us in our room asap, as she saw us arrive by bike, and assumed we were exhausted. Our room was not impressive (I don't recommend room 3), but we asked to move and were accommodated without drama. Room 2 was a huge improvement, with its 4 post bed and well arranged furniture. The hotel staff were very warm and friendly. Continental breakfast was more than enough to eat, and featured fresh croissants. Their grounds are lovely, and away from the hustle and bustle. One note for bikers; they have a sheltered bike rack (converted horse shelter), which is a huge plus. Now, the restaurant: to start, we were given 50% off our bottle of wine because we were hotel guests. The food was just plain amazing. I had the filet, my girlfriend the duck. We had sweetbreads as an appetizer. It was the best meal I've had since eating at Marigold (in West Philadelphia), which is considerably more expensive. Everything was prepared exquisitely. I can't understand the bad food reviews, except to say that no meat in any French restaurant should ever be ordered above medium, or prepare for disappointment. French meats should be consumed rare to raw. In all, we had a lovely weekend with lovely hosts, and would repeat the experience anytime.

As an East Falls resident, I was excited to check out In Riva and was really hoping it would be as great as it seemed. Fortunately, it was. My meal there was fantastic. For starters, the ambiance of the place is really nice. Cool lighting setup, cute little bar at the front of the restaurant, and a big balcony outside that overlooks the Schuylkill and will be great in the spring. 

The meal started with a complimentary dish of toasted (i think?) nuts that was really tasty and a welcome alternative to the usual basket of bread. We ordered the spicy mussels, which came with a nice, buttery, crusty bread for dipping in the sauce. The sauce, while really tasty, was not really spicy -- my only complaint. 

Our main dish was the cippollini pizza: pancetta, brussel sprouts, goat cheese. An absolutely delicious mix of sweet, salty, and spicy. I loved it. The pizza had a nice char from the wood-fired oven but the crust still remained chewy. 

I do think the restaurant is still figuring itself out a bit. We were sitting at a bar overlooking the kitchen, and our server openly admitted to having a rough time serving us in that area. Also, they serve the pizza on top of a big can of tomatoes, which looks cool, but when the guy brought our pizza he said "watch out, the plate is really hot and unsteady." Not really the best combo; they might want to rethink that. 

However, neither of those things were really a deterrent for me and I will definitely be back. So happy In Riva is here!

Great crafted burgers and a great balance of meat to other ingredients. The Ramsay Pimento Cheese Burger was fantastic. I usually don't enjoy ice burg lettuce on a burger, but it was really great, paired with the aioli, pickles, and bacon. The house fries are also a great choice, and in general, some of the best in town. 

The Mac'n Cheese bites are fantastic! Great crunch and flavor when you bite into them. They are served with their house honey mustard and maple ketchup. Unfortunately, neither of them pair particularly well with the cheese bites. Definitely worth getting them to try!

Good drafts available. I recommend the Blackberry Farm Saison, which is has a light profile with slightly complex overtones. 

I rate Burger Up as better than Burger Republic, and just shy of The Pharmacy. Best burger in 12th South!

Other Notes: The service was great at the bar on a Saturday evening. Friendly staff. Bar itself seemed a little high from the height of the bar stools. Environment is nicely dimmed and they had great music selection through the entire night. No TVs.

Ok so I went to this place several months ago, maybe January? And can't believe I haven't left a review yet. To be honest I don't remember the exact name of my dish but it was some type of truffle bucatini. There are no words. Just incredible. In full disclosure I'm a sucker for truffle anything, and pasta, so this was kind of a no brainer. Can't wait to go back now that it's nice out!

My wife and I really enjoyed this place.  The wait staff was super friendly and helpful.  The dishes we tried were really good.  My favorite was the roasted dates with with pork belly and blue cheese.  My wife lived the mussels in white wine sauce.

Some portions were a bit small for what you payed for them.  They charge $2 for four very small pieces of plain bread for dipping.

Overall it was a great experience and would recommend it to other looking for a unique place in Nashville.

I was at Jon's the day after Thanksgiving with my brother and his girlfriend. After wandering around Society Hill and South Street, we were tired and hungry and wanted to eat somewhere decent. I had seen this place a bunch of times and thought it might be worth checking out, since they claimed that famed Three Stooges member Larry Fine was born where there restaurant now stands. 

We sat outside on the patio and waited. And waited. And waited some more. Granted waiting 20 minutes for a simple hello at a restaurant, is not something I normally do. But we were starving and didn't feel like wandering around much. Nearly some thirty minutes after we sat down, we were finally acknowledged and asked what we would like to drink. The drinks then took nearly 15 more minutes to arrive, before we even got to place an order.

Our food took forever to come out from the kitchen. Our server wasn't all that personable or apologetic for the slowness. She even forgot my soup that I ordered. I can't recall everything we ordered, but my sandwich was nothing special, and not all that hot as I recall. My guess is that it sat under a heat lamp for a few minutes before arriving at the table.

It took over an hour to get seated, be greeted, get a drink, and then get our food. It was much longer than I normally have waited for lackluster service and average tasting food. I wanted to ask for a manager to complain, but didn't feel like waiting another hour to find one. What a shame, they have a great corner location, an interesting history with the Larry Fine angle, but they need better servers and better food quality.

Took the Grapes N Hops tour with Shawn.  My wife and I had a fantastic time!  There were three wineries and a stop at Figueroa Brewing to end the tour.  Sogno del Fiori was our favorite stop.  The owner is very cordial and has a true depth of knowledge reagarding all aspects of wine.  We had a great time on the tour and I would highly recommend this company.

Target is a big chain store filled with a wide selection of clothing, electronics, housewares, health & beauty items, cleaning supplies, and even groceries (in some locations), and on and on. As my sister likes to say, "Target is where America shops for stuff". If I'm doing a general shopping trip, then Target is a great place to look for most of the items on my list.

This Target is located in the northern end of the shopping center at N. Dale Mabry and Ehrlich. I guess it's true that each store echos the needs of the local community since I prefer the selection at the bigger Super Target on W. Hillsborough which is near to Westchase. This store seems to appeal to an older audience with established families, and that's not me.

Since I was shopping for an exciting list of items like plastic trash bags, laundry detergent, and assorted housewares I opted for the convenience of this store, and found everything I needed. The store is clean, the aisles wide, but the checkout process is generally slow.

I've been here countless times and tried numerous treats, from cookies and other baked goods to cakes and chocolate covered pretzels, and I've never been disappointed!
Just look at the beautiful cake in the photo- it was such a hit at Easter dinner. The chocolate icing and hard chocolate covering was delicious and the vanilla cake inside was the perfect consistency. 
And for Thanksgiving, there is no better choice than the double crust apple pie- to die for! 
Lovely staff, especially the students working there- they are always nice!

For the first time for Mother's Day, my hubby took me to the Civic Theatre for Les Mis.  I have seen it three other times and I was blown away!  The theater is a great size and all the ticket prices were the same and somehow he managed to get us fabulous second row middle and I could see the lines in the actors faces as they sang my favorite songs. During the final scene when the rebels are killed, I was so close I could watch for them to take a breath (they didn't!).  It was incredible how well done this show was.  The sound was AMAZING, the orchestra blew me away and the intimacy of the theater was awesome!

I would definitely be back to see another show.  They host an amazing array of choices throughout the year for affordable prices and they serve snacks, beer/wine and soda/waters upon entering.  It's easy to get parking and it's very simple to find. The theater have a program for kids who are interested in the stage and they offer local actors great opportunities.  

Other than being a little chilly (bring a sweater, ladies), it was a perfect experience.  I truly think this is a great place for anyone to see a show live.  It is accessible, easy and affordable.  Don't miss out on this if you enjoy theater.  I am looking forward to the next time...

Checked this out with the boyfriend and his parents. After watching Hubert on top 
Chef masters, really wanted to try some of his handy-work! 

Kobe burger w/ Swiss was so good! But boyfriend ordered his medium and it was a little too well done. Think my medium rare was definitely better. Sweet potato fries were good and the zucchini buttermilk Fred were extra tasty! 

Service was good but a little scattered..but boyfriend LOVED the cheesecake 'burger' on a donut. A little much for me..but he was a happy camper ! 

Overall..very good. But not sure it was as good as I hoped considering Hubert's skill level...

At age 53, this was my first trip ever to New Orleans.  WOW! I fell in love and it was quite overwhelming to know which stores to shop.  So much choice!  My strategy was to make the rounds and at the end go back to what I liked most.  HOWEVER, the New Orleans spirits had something else in mind for me!  Third store in on Royal Street was Vintage 329.  I tried on a cool vintage ring and said to "Jamie" the lovely young woman who was helping me: "Love it, but need to look at other stores first.  See you later maybe?"  Then a pair of earrings caught my eye.   She pulled them out.  We started talking about history and then I saw a necklace I just had to try on -  and from that point on I was HOOKED!  We had so much FUN "playing."  We chatted it up about the various histories of vintage jewelry in the store; I tried lots of things on (even a tiara); I walked around the store and admired myself in the mirror with various pieces; Jamie gave me awesome feedback and helped me decide which pieces suited me most.  It was an all around BLAST!!!  I loved reveling in the awesome vintage jewelry and imagining who made it and who wore it before me.  I delighted in the time spent with Jamie.  It was all so playful, uplifting. fun AND educational!  Can you believe I purchased SEVEN gorgeous, amazing, pieces (including the tiara) AND Jamie gave me a special magical gift to boot.  Oh, and Jamie also prepared historic write-ups for each piece including a vintage advertisement that a brooch I purchased was featured in.  Sooooo happy :)
Love this place!  Friendly, great food, and great prices!  Always specials going on too! Down home genuine place! Kid friendly too.

The main feature- fried chicken, was not remarkable.  Many other places in town have better.  The mashed potatoes did not seem to be made from scratch, surprising for the price point of this place.  Apparently it is too much effort to have their bread basket for lunch, which is unfortunate, because it probably was their best item, had it been available.

Raving review from Californian outsider!

I came by for lunch during one of the many crowded conferences I'm sure St. Louis gets (holler, Urbana12!). My friend and I found seats at the bar as others were clearing out (got kind of lucky there), and our server was a delightfully facial haired man who walked us through menu selections and sassed me like we were best friends.

I'm kind of a cheapo, so the pricey burgers were at first a turn off, but I had heard very good things about their specialty burgers from other friends. I helped myself to the basic burger, which I asked for cooked all the way, and was pleasantly not dry at all. You know what else was delightful? Their homemade ketchup! Perfectly sweet and perfectly ketchupy.

The order did take a bit longer to come out than I would have liked, but watching my sassy non-robot server make lots of different drinks for other customers ameliorated the pain of the wait. Thanks Bailey's Range, I'll miss you forever.
Tried this place for the first time today food is outstanding. Service was great as well. I will definitely be back.

I paid for a room at the Peppermill 3 months before I arrived for 3 people, 2 double beds. On Arrival ( Thursday afternoon ) I was told they were very sorry but they only had rooms with 1 king-size bed, but I could have a rollaway. The first room was so small that the roll away could not be open. The second room was ok but a rollaway cot for an 11 night reservation. Finally on the 4th day they would try and move us. I went to the front desk to ask when the room would be available, a very nice women at reception said let me get my manager and see if we can do something for you? I did not ask for anything other than a room for myself and my family, one that we could all have at least a part of a bed. I was basically yelled at by the hotel manager, Sorry it was either Melinda, MaryAnn or Lori. Now I did not ask for compensation I just wanted the room I had paid for. Do yourself a favor DON'T STAY HERE!

I hadn't been to Luke in many years, so the other night a friend was staying at a hotel nearby and I suggested we go to Luke for dinner. I was disappointed that they only had one of the five selections of oysters, however we enjoyed some tasty P&J's oysters as an appetizer. We moved on to order the Shrimp and Crawfish Etouffee and the Crispy Brussels Sprouts. The etouffee was excellent, not too spicy on the cajun side and just right on the creole. I look forward to exploring more of their menu soon.

I am getting ready for our trip to New Orleans this Halloween and was just fantasizing about our last trip there and how we ate at Muriels and it was wonderful.

For a place in the quarter that is right in the center of tourist land, this restaurant is classy but not overly stuffy. The atmosphere is beautiful. The walls, a deep velvety maroon with a collection of antiques and gorgeous New Orleans decor. You can see the attention to detail. There are no spots on the water glasses or silver. The table cloths are immaculate.

There is nothing too complicated on the menu, just delicious Cajun & Creole food. There is a table d'hote option which I like because you get a full course meal for one price. The wine selection is broad and desserts are heavenly. The bread they bring to your table is unbelievably soft and warm and served with an herb butter. 

A reservation is recommended but there are times when you can walk in for lunch or dinner also. It is an expansive restaurant in a gorgeous french quarter building. Appropriate attire should be worn (no shorts and flip flops) but it does not require a sport coat. I like to wear a dress to dinner anyways, there is something about fancy New Orleans dining that calls for being dressed pretty. If you are wearing a ball cap they will ask you to remove it and I appreciate that. I like that they maintain their standards and hold strong to those policies. If you want to eat in your outside clothes, go to an oyster house. Please, have respect for yourself and the other diners. : )

We have had beautiful, consistent food, every time, with some of the best service we've ever had anywhere. The servers are never hurried or rushed or nervous, but work at a relaxed pace. The servers, runners and bussers work as a tight ship and you can see the quality in their work. Everything comes out at the right time. Dishes are cleared at the right time. Water is filled at the right time. It is 100% perfect service.

A warning..... this place is haunted by a man who lost his home in a gamble. The restaurant is the ghosts former home. I was in the ladies room alone and something had turned the lights off on me while I was in the loo. There was no one else in the room with me. Scary but interesting to say the least.

I really enjoyed this place and my boyfriend did too. I would recommend it time and again for anyone in the quarter who wants fine dining, but not too-fine of dining.

Stopped in for a late lunch upon arrival. We were famished. Our server was on the case and he took great care of us. Made recommendations regarding menu items and drink suggestions--everything spot on. My oysters were fresh and tasty. The boiled shrimp were incredible--a huge portion and SO fresh. Crab cakes were big and crisp. Loved my cup of gumbo as well. Even though it was hot outside and all the windows were open, it was nice and cool inside due to the many large overhead fans. Go here.

Coffee and rescue cats make a wonderful combination. A great  café with delicious coffee and a small selection of treats. I got the mint Oreo cookie brownie and it was off the hook delicious. They also have a nice selection of teas, hot chocolate etc. They also have cool cat gifts ( cat champagne)  The cats are in a different room that is monitors by " chaperone" which is such a good idea to make Sure everyone is treating the cats well and also she will tell you about any cat in the room. The owners of the café are very friendly and very passionate about what they do. To date they have already rehomed over 30 cats. What a wonderful cause. I would highly recommend this place

We always like Safeway.  The store is smaller then the larger Fry's in the neighborhood and it is easier to find what you want with out all the crowds.  We also prefer there flower and balloon selection.  The employees are great and always friendly.  We also like the US Bank on the inside.

Rude rude rude!!!! I've dealt with the service center twice now.  Originally I work with Joe and he was great (didn't work with him the seconds visit)but I had to take my car back a week later and from booking the appointment to dropping my car off everyone was extremely rude. I ended up telling them I'd be going to a different dealer and will never be returning. 
I ended up go to a different Hyundai dealer and it took the mechanic 5 mins to figure the problem out and order me a new radio.

We went on our first cruise with Carnival and had an excellent time!  The food was delicious, drinks were excellent, staff was friendly and accommodating and the activities (trivia, etc) were fun!  Spa services were a bit overpriced but I expected that.  I have food allergies and the dining staff took great care of me customizing meals I could eat.   Though I have no comparison, the rooms seemed fine to me - clean, nicely designed.  Our only complaint was that we purchased the inclusive, unlimited drink package, which indeed had a limit of 10 drinks per person per day.  I tend to choose inclusive vacations and have never been given a limit.  Ten drinks may be fine for some, but when you think you may want a mimosa with breakfast, monitors or beer by the pool, wine with dinner and then drinks at the show or while at the bars, that adds up to 10 rapidly.  I did have a good time and would do it again,  it would probably explore other lines with truly unlimited packages first.

Beautiful setting but WAY overpriced for average Mexican food. Meat was dry and bland. Miguel's, Taco Bus and Poblanos are all better. The servers were quite friendly however my husbands drink order was incorrect as well as an entree ingredient.
Decent food, decent amounts. Just order a few different plates and share with the others at the table.

I would have loved to write a positive review about this restaurant, however, the hostess at the door did not give us the opportunity to do so. I have never been treated in such manner. She shoved us out the door and behaved very hostile towards me and my group of friends. As a client, I recommend that you treat your customers. If this were my restaurant I would not tolerate a staff member who rages at clients, instead of handling the situation in a discrete manner. Never coming back.

Great music, great food, great bartenders, great location.... It's a pretty amazing place. The fish tacos are BOMB, the St.Germain cocktail is my favorite. I love the fact that they have outdoor seating which makes best for people watching. Must go if your visiting downtown St Pete aka the burg!!!

I LOVE THIS PLACE. The instructors are great, the owner is such a sweetheart, the classes are challenging, the other students are positive and nice and I always feel comfortable there. The schedule works great for me and all the yin offered is really doing wonders for me. Did I mention I LOVE IT HERE?? Also, she does some great offers, like $30 for your first month unlimited! How can you say no to that?

I'm usually at Ulta shopper but since moving to the city Sephora is perfect! They have so much stuff you could spend hours here! They have all your cosmetic needs under one roof! And you have plenty opportunities to sample anything you want!

The definition of a 5 star restaurant.  (I know I grade easy, but if I was a food critic from the New York Times, I would still call this place 5 star).  It's not cheap so bring your money, but the food is WORTH it.  Oh and also, there's an in-house ghost.  Yeah that's right, dinner and a ghost.

Its good, not great.
Just not my favorite tasting chinese.
The lunch combos are a good deal. They come with soup & an egg roll. Ive had the generals chicken, sesame chicken, beef broccoli, sweet and sour chicken, the shrimp chow me in, hourse fried rice, egg drop soup, and the hot and sour soup. Not all at once! But, its just kinda....meh. Nothing is super good where I want to come back.. 
Ill eat there if I'm with a group that wants to go, but its not my #1.

Darn awesome. Love the ambiance, love the food, love the music. My father even drank whiskey here and loved it, which is just crazy making. Also very friendly and fun bartenders/staff. Highly recommended.

Only downside - it gets packed, and there's really no place to wait.
Decided to treat my mom here for a birthday present! We were extremely impressed with our shellac mani and pedi - not to mention the customer service and attention to detail was superior.

I called for a ride to the Amtrak station over and hour ahead of time.  I should have read the reviews ahead of time. The cab never showed.  I kept calling and was told over and over again it would be there in five minutes.  Needless to say, I missed the train to Chicago.  Someone should open a reliable taxi service.  The other companies didn't even answer the phone but this is far worse.  They lie about picking you up.  I could have walked the five miles and saved myself a ton of aggravation.  One star is way too many.

I'm a huge fan of Mellow Mushroom!  I've been to at least 3 different ones in Atlanta, along with one in Winston-Salem, Raleigh, and Greenville, NC.  We love their pretzel appetizers, caesar, greek, and pepperoni pizza.  And the beer selection is always great.  But for some reason, the Brandon location has struggled on service.  The waitress we had was "out there".  We had to constantly remind her of drink refills.  And then we sat and watched our pizzas sit on the shelf for 10 minutes after coming out of the oven...while she ran the take-out register and chatted up the bartender.  The food was just as good as other locations...but the service...c'mon...customers visiting a pizza shop don't have high expectations to begin with.  I've had wet sponges with more personality.  They've got the food quality and kitchen staff...get rid of the service problems and this Mellow Mushroom will be the best in the pizza business for the Tampa area.

Taco Tuesdays is my jam! The line type serving is a lot o like chipotle, but the tacos are better. I believe I got the tacos with all of the dressings on top. Highly recommend if you want to get a quick bite to eat downtown. There isn't a lot of seating when it gets super busy, however if you come at a non peak time you won't have any issues. 

Unlike a few other taco shops you can take a handful of chips from a heated machine, which is a nice touch. Choose your own salsa and refill your own drinks. You can also get beer here which is a nice touch when you're having a quick taco any day of the week. 

The atmosphere is pretty much expected for a taco place, and the price is great for what you get. I've only been here once, but recommend if you're in the area and need a quick bite to eat.

As mentioned by other Yelpers the food, location and wonderful decor are standout but what sets Clear Sky on Cleveland (CSC) apart is Service with a capital S.  

My mission was to hit the CSC happy hour and then catch a show at the Capitol theater across the street after driving in rush hour traffic from Orlando.

I looked at my watch as I crossed the threshold and it was 5:58 with happy hour ending at 6 pm.  The host directed me to the bar for the fastest service and the server quickly placed my order of drinks and appetizers.  For the record happy hour is 2-6 pm and they offer drink specials and half priced hummus, falafels and naan (flat) breads.

We got there just at shift change and as we sat at the bar, Kayla took over as our server.  I was a little concerned because of the previous server's efficiency but Kayla is a star.  She is the perfect combination of efficiency, helpful and is charming - just fun to be around.  She helped describe menu items, she offered info and when I made a bad choice (she had provided info but I had already made up my mind) removed the item from my check.

Here is what we ended up with.  They have 8 naan flat breads and we chose the sausage and broccolini as well as the mushroom and herb.  Both outstanding choices and I could not pick a favorite.  We also got the hummus which was excellent but very filling.

I ordered the cottage pie and it was not to my liking.  I think they could have a better title but it was more like a stew as Kayla had mentioned with a lump of mashed in the middle.  It had a lot of celery and did not match my Irish idea of cottage pie.

So here is the break down:

Pro
-Great food - lots of apps as well as entrees, burger, sandwiches and flatbreads.  I think there are a lot of appetizers and picking several apps is the way to go especially with groups.  There are many interesting choices.
-Good wine - generous pours even at happy hour and the wine is good quality
-Interior decor and al fresco dining is modern, clean and interesting.  The bathrooms were spotless and decoration of the stalls is fun
-Happy hour offers food and wine at really great prices
-Service and really caring about the customers.  After I ordered an item and sent it back they comp'd me a piece of pie for dessert.  I mean I felt bad for sending something back and they went over the top to make it right.  I dine out a lot and this is exceptional

Cons
-There is a concert venue across the street.  It was quiet when we got there but I saw the place quickly fill up and the crowd cleared out right before the show.  Plan accordingly for the best service. 
-They have a lot in back and there is on street parking with meters until 6 pm.  Again with the concert venue I could see parking a block or so away and walking.  It's worth it.  Ruth Eckerd uses the Captiol Theater for smaller venue shows.  

We have another trip planned to Clearwater and I will go out of the way to dine at Clear Sky on Cleveland once again.
We came late on a Sunday as all other places were closed.  We were treated like family and had the most delicious garlic rocks, pizza, calzone, and cannoli.  Best service and friendly atmosphere.

Not impressed. I understand only having 4 treadmills when starting out, but this little place is jam packed around 5PM and there is nothing available. Then they take out an additional $25 on top of your membership every few months and take suggestions on a new piece of equipment although I'm not sure where they plan on putting all this stuff. I think it's overpriced as well. The staff is friendly and helpful. I would recommend going in the mornings as it is empty between 6-8.
Caln pizza is better, this joints ok for pizza I do wonder if they make up for there mediocracy with hogies. Great selection of beer to-go.

Above average food in a cute and eclectic atmosphere. Server was very attentive and overall good experience. I ordered the seafood tagliatelle pasta and my husband got the salmon. The pasta dish was the favorite of the two.

Great spot in the heart of the French Quarter. Do yourself a favor and don't consider ordering anything other than the BBQ shrimp. If you look up the recipe, it's shrimp that's DROWNING in a flavorful butter sauce and, as you'd expect, it's AMAZING. Worth a stop for lunch or dinner when you're in NOLA.
The food and pricing was fine. However, there was a picture of Trump and a positive article about him taped to the wall. I don't go to restaurants with a political view.
Nice rooms and shower pressure was great. Check in was fast and staff is friendly. Free breakfast. Hotel is right near the on / off ramp of the interstate. So its very easy to get to.

Food was ok. Seemed to lack flavor. Potato salad was blah. They forgot to use our free Appetizer Yelp coupon. But since husbAnd checked us out I shouldn't complain. But it was a slow Sunday so not sure why.  Lots of other options on the river front to try.  So in general not great but not horrible.

I feel like such a snot complaining about a Starbucks. The staff here is great. My issue here is the guests. There are a couple people that live here. So if you were planning on sitting in one of the cozy chairs think again. They've basically claimed them as their own. Take a close look and you can see their ass prints in each seat. Seriously. And on a nice afternoon there's usually 5-10 too many highschoolers hanging around. They tend to sit outside around the Cold Stone next door which is a little bit of a relief. Where do these kids get money for Starbucks everyday? I was counting change to share a $1 slice at the local pizzeria! But otherwise, drinks made right- every time- also friendly and quick drive-thru.

Celebrated Cinco de Mayo here with a friend recently and it was a good time!  Although the place was super crowded (as to be expected) we were able to grab our drinks from the bar and snag a table in the same area.  We both ordered frozen margaritas and they were pretty strong!

Cute restaurant and great location. Service was poor. Waitress took 15 minutes to greet us and get our drink orders. Would have been okay, but she had slight attitude the rest of the night and made us seem more like a burden. Food was good. Not great, but good! Also, it was uncomfortably chilly, so bring a jacket.

Dr. Gramling is AMAZING!  She takes the time so that you understand your pet's health and provides great advice and recommendations.  I couldn't believe how much time she spent explaining our sweet Kai's kidney problem, the numbers and tests and what are options were.  She and her staff are the best in the area.  I have been to many other vets and have gone to her for the past 4 years!
So happy with my first experience here... came today (Saturday) around 5 for my first SNS mani. They have so many color options, and the woman really took her time to make my nails perf!
Nice cafeteria like place. The menu is very limited. It's a different take on tacos. Kind of like southern food in a soft taco shell. The shrimp corn chowder soup was delish also.

Finally got a chance to try this place and I'm so glad I did! I went for the elote (Mexican corn) that I heard about and was happy that it was just as tasty and delicious as any I've had before.
