Pasta dishes were good and generous portion.

Overall, service was fast and food reasonable but ambience was a bit creepy.

Best car buying experience ever! This is my 5th car purchase and this was by far one of the easiest and they didn't steamroll me or try to get me into more car than I needed. 

I got the car I have been looking at for some time now, and in a rare color which is totally awesome! The process was painless and the interest rate was lower than I expected, not to mention they called me to come in and sign new paperwork when they got me an even lower rate than originally quoted! 

If the service is bad or I have trouble with the extended warranty I'll be sure to update, but so far so good.

This place has amazing happy hour! I didn't order anything from the regular menu so this review is for happy hour menu only. 

There was a large group of us so we just ordered one of each off the happy hour menu. Many of the dishes come in three and four pieces so sharing is caring! 

The bacon jam, pretzel with beer cheese, pork rinds, house chips with buffalo sauce and flatbread stood out from the rest. 

The bacon jam is super flavorful! The pretzels were soft and the beer cheese paired nicely. The pork rinds were the star of the show IMO. Crispy, light, and perfectly dusted with your choice of flavor. The house chips were airy and crisp as well and who doesn't love food covered in buffalo and blue cheese?! The flatbread presented more as a pizza but I just loved the crispness to it. It's what all thin crust pizzas should strive to be. 

We also drank...a lot. I loved the lemon flavored drink on the happy hour menu and the dirty martini!  Both were $6 each. I mean. Can you really beat that?! 

Service was on point. Especially with our large group of crazies. Would definitely recommend!

A friend of mine was guest bartending one evening, so I decided to give PH a shot. All drinks were half price (hell yes)! I think the appetizers were cheaper also, but I vaguely remember eating the hummus since I was pretty drunk. The atmosphere wasn't my usual, but it was cool mingling with Philly's 9-5er's.
I did not expect this random Taiwanese restaurant outside of Circus Circus was actually REALLY GOOD for American-Taiwanese food standard. Get the braided pork bowl and rolled pancakes.

Love love love Sprouts! I'm so happy it's only a ten minute drive from my house. The 99 cent lemon snaps and apple crisps are to die for, as well as the double chocolate muffins. Oh and the sweet potatoes are the best I've ever had. I will definitely become a regular at this grocery store.

I came here to eat after moving my boyfriend into his apartment. I love the interior and the vibe was friendly and active. Lots of people at 11 pm on a Saturday night, although they came in waves. I was afraid their kitchen would be closed but I'm so glad it wasn't! I ordered the beef sandwich and it came in a reasonable amount of time. The sandwich was a respectable size and quite delicious. Their fries are to die for!!! Shoestring with just the right texture and amount of salt. 
My bf and his family were drinking, and I was impressed with how friendly the bar staff was. They were more than happy to explain to us their beer selection and gave us samples often! They were always attentive, despite the busy hour, and our drinks were quickly replenished. I would gladly come here again.

Zimmer's Seafood, located at an underdeveloped pedestrian friendly intersection in the heart of Voscoville, prepares arguably the best dressed shrimp po-boy in town (Castnet's are very good as well). You pay for quality here as Zimmer's is not the cheapest but we want real shrimp not the dried bite sized variety right? Of course. My only gripe is that they are closed on Sundays in opposition to my stomach's occasional Sunday po-boy craving. Check it out!

The food was superb and the menu was classic bistro with flair (though the menu itself had a coffee stain on the back). My wife and I shared a French onion soup that was comme il faut (the wife would have liked more cheese, but then she's from Wisconsin). For the main course, we shared the steak frites. The 10oz NY steak was a perfect medium rare, and very tender, especially for a NY cut. The frites were simply perfect.
   The service was another story. We arrived at 5:00 pm on a Tuesday and had the place to ourselves until we were nearly finished. The decor is also great, btw: airy, light, and clean. But something happens to servers in Tucson when they land a job at a real restaurant. They can turn into insufferably condescending, attitude-stricken, unctuous, pompous twits. And yet, somehow, also obsequious. That said, the food did come out mostly on time, and we did have the attention of our server when we needed him (and then some). Please take my word on this, so I don't have to re-live the ludicrous dialogue.
   As for the prices, $21 seems high for steak frites. This dish is a stand-by in France, where perfection of preparation is expected, not surprising. And vegetables would have been another $4 each. The special was a salmon burger, which also seemed high at $20, even if it were the best you ever ate. 
   Augustin Brasserie is a welcome contribution to fine dining in Tucson. The food, which is after all the main thing, is terrific. The very possibility of roasted bone marrow makes my heart soar. But please, drop the attitude.
Just moved to Philadelphia and I can't stop ordering from here!  The Wonton Soup and Pork Dumplings are so great.

Where to start? Great landscaping, public art, tennis courts, playgrounds, handball and racquetball courts, water features. Earlier reviews noted the courts needed resurfacing and I think it's been done since then. The bathrooms are also usually quite clean. Dog walkers are provided poop bags, even. The architecture around the park is gorgeous art deco, too, which is a boon for walkers and runners. There are several notable events in the park that amount to strong programming (tree lighting for winter, the local church has a picnic, and there are regular music concerts). Francis is in the top five of great city parks in a city of more than 100.

Came in with my family of three and ordered very simple entree's. The server was nice though had to repeatedly tell us our food was on its way. An hour later after notifying management of our displeasure our meal comes out a cheesesteak,salad, and pasta dish. Eager to finally eat they screwed up the pasta dish and by then I was fed up and told them I'm not happy and will not eat anything else on there menu. All they did was take that pasta dish cost off the check. That is very unacceptable customer service. I would be very careful about going to this establishment. Unacceptable!!!
Good experience. We sat at the bar and had great service. Drinks were on point. Split a Jackson burger and fries with gravy. Both were tasty. We will be back.
First time costumer and i really enjoyed myself, good staff and very clean, great flavors but i still felt there could have been more, but that's me.

This is a romantic, Italian restaurant! I was thrilled to get a booth next to the window on M street. I love to people watch. I loved the Cabernet the waiter recommended to go with a our wagyu steaks and tagliatelle pasta. That pasta was AMAZING!
Love this place! Great patio area, great bartenders, and great drinks. My go to starter spot!

First time paddleboarding. 3 women from the East Coast..so we were nervous. We were newbies to paddleboarding.

Grant was our instructor and he was amazing and patient and has the best Aussie accent (it's real too!). We had great instruction on the ground and safety instruction before hitting the water. We did really well and owe it all to Grant and his individual attention and not pushing us beyond our capabilities. We ventured farther out to sea where the waters were a little bumpy and we were just determined to stay standing. 2 of us fell numerous times but had the best time. Grant brought lunch from Trader Joe's. yum. we loved it. We woud recommend this company and Grant to everyone; in fact, we already have shared it with others.

I tried to order the Mediterranean chicken dinner, which is listed on the menu. The employee behind the counter told me they no longer served that there, only salmon and steak. I asked if she meant they were out of chicken for the day. No, she said, they just don't serve it any longer. I left and went to the Vets location instead.
Love this place!  I always get one of the pasta specials or the pescatore in white sauce over linguine.

This was the WORST damn food I ever had I had four starving kids at the house after my food showed up late and my total was different than what GrubHub said it was, it was more in fact I had no fries with my burgers and the owner hung up on me several times I explained there were no fries and I had a diabetic child here and he told me she could eat the burger my son found a hair on his Burger and the anchovy pizza tasted like a piece of rubber I have pictures to show that we threw our food in the trash can there was a Squirt of some mayonnaise little bits of tomatoes and brown chunks of lettuce the guy on the phone who claimed to be the owner and manzger was the rudest piece of crap I've ever heard in my life. 44.00 for 3 sbitty burgers with no fries now its 11:30 and I'm ordering pizza from Papa John's so my child can eat and take insulin .

My husband and I were impressed! We got a great "Labor Day" rate, so we thought we would give it a try. 

Great location, close to campus and a quick walk to downtown. It was perfect for us. The room was spacious & clean. 

A huge pet peeve of mine is having the sink/mirror IN the bathroom. It was...so that was a disappointment. I can't get ready while my husband is showering/potty etc. 

Other than that, big windows that open, the bed was comfy enough, and again it felt very very clean.
Huge oysters when I was there.  Great service!  Had a muffuletta  (half).  It was all very tasty!

Definitely the best you are gonna get for an airport hotel. The room was clean, spacious and comfortable. Check in was easy but the desk staff told me they had overbooked the hotel- fortunately I'm a starwoods member so they guaranteed my room. That is why only 4 stars, I would've been really angry if I made a reservation only to find out it was overbooked... Overall good value if you have an early flight and classic w.  We had always stayed in the Sheraton before our flights but I'll be staying at aloft from now on. It was less expensive, rooms were cleaner, staff were friendlier and all around it's a better value. I wouldn't spend more than one night in any of the airport hotels- there are so many better places in better neighborhoods - but this is super convenient if trying to catch an early flight. Shuttle worked out great!

I stopped by Bier last night for a networking event.  The staff were very friendly and helpful.  I sampled three beers: The Belgian Blonde, John's Porter, and Barley Buddy Brown.  John's Porter was my favorite.  There are several seating options including large tables and comfy chairs.  I would definitely return!
Good food...strange atmosphere but we will definitely go back

$2 pizza rossa in America, but it tastes like shitty monsanto American agribusiness tomatoes, but they have Leffe. Given that they are making huge American pizza and reheating it to order, they do it pretty well, but the ingredients are not very high quality.
Great place for big groups. Friendly service, I asked for what they recommended and they were 100 % on point. You can pretty much customize anything you order. Bathroom smells amazing, lol...

IHOP is the place to go for a family bunch 
There pancakes are a special recipe. There eggs and bacon make the pancakes even better! For the grown ups you have a sissy mix of red peppers, potatoes, bacon, and a toasted piece of bread 

Go with your family to ihop!!!

Great Indian food! We received a basket of crispy crackers with four different chutneys to try as well as complimentary red pepper soup prior to our meal. My mango lassi was the perfect level of sweet and refreshing. My friend and I shared the palak paneer (and I'm looking forward to the leftovers tonight!) and the chicken shahi korma, a dish that was new to both of us...and there were no leftovers of that! It was wonderful. Both dishes were served with a side of basmati rice, and the attentive waiter offered to bring us more if we'd like. Excellent food, great value! I can't wait to try out the lunch buffet one day.

Spur of the moment decision to eat there last night - we dined in. Am happy we tried it. The steamed dumplings were delicious. The pork egg foo young was absolutely delicious. I could definitely taste it was fresh and made on the spot, not pre-made and frozen. For once, I could actually taste the egg. My husband had the pork lo mein, and he gave it a thumb's up. No, it's not NYC.... Come on people....accept that you live in Tampa Bay and judge accordingly. China City is not the prettiest of places, but hey, I find that holes-in-the-wall stay in business because the food speaks for itself.

I bought a groupon for One haircut, style and conditioning for $79 and can't use it because i had made an appointment but had to cancel 4 hours before because I had family emergency. They told me that it required 24 hours to cancel which is not stated anywhere in the groupon itself. Also had problem with them before when they did not let me use the amount I paid for and groupon had expired.

Luke's was one of our favorite meals in New Orleans. Our only problem was I made reservations on Open Table, we get there and after about a 15 minute wait at the bar, we were seated at a table for two in the back by where the waiters come in and out. My husband was not happy and after asking a couple of times we were moved to another table for two (there were several) more to the center of the restaurant.

The Louisiana Rabbit and Chicken Liver Pate was wonderful and we loved all the sides that went along with it. The manager has since sent me the recipe that is used at that restaurant and also his Provence restaurant. Can't wait to try it.

I have also recreated the Salad Luke. I loved the presentation of this salad. I made my own pickled yellow beets and added beets to the different layers instead of just on the bottom of the salad. 

The black drum with the meunier sauce was also wonderful as was the lemon cheesecake with lemon sorbet for dessert.

We could have stopped eating after the pate but we surged on. They brought more crostini and it was just hard to quit eating the stuff.

The single gem on south street

Tons of beers on tap or bottled 

But what no one knows is that they also have the best wings and cheese steak egg rolls on south street. 

Juke box, and upstairs has live music often

I had wanted to visit Bella Pizzeria for quite a while. Located in a rather large strip center on East 82nd Street just East of Keystone at the Crossing, Bella Pizza is a four-location indiana mini-chain with locations in Keystone, Hamilton Town Center, Clay Terrace, and in Kokomo. Self-dubbed as a "New York Style Eatery," one can only assume it's because the restaurant tends to be dirty as it's certainly not a description of the pizza. 

Okay, I'm sorry. That was a tad too snarky. 

Bella offers pizza by the slice along with whole pies along with calzones, pasta, salads, breadsticks, a kids menu and some desserts. The location is next to a Mattress Firm  and not too far from Maggie Moo's. It happens to have a couple of accessible parking spots right in front of it, and while they're not quite ADA compliant I'd suspect most people won't have any trouble with them. You enter the front door and head straight toward an ordering counter. They do serve up several specials. I found their slice prices to be pretty workable, though I wasn't as impressed with their whole pie prices. They do offer delivery. 

I ordered a slice of sausage pizza, two pepperoni breadsticks and a large fountain drink. They do have Gold Peak iced tea, so that was a definite plus. My entire meal came in at just over $7 - certainly less than you'll pay for mall pizza, though this isn't a mall and they sure don't have the convenience factor going on. You can actually order online. 

I will admit that considering their location I'd expect it to be a lot nicer inside Bella. Yes, you have multiple tables where you can sit down and enjoy the meal and they certainly are decked out in the usual New York urban decor, think a grittier Subway, but it all seemed a lot more kitsch than I expected. 

I've seen a couple Yelp reviews refer to Bella's pizza as glorified mall pizza and, quite honestly, that's an accurate description. The sausage was chunked, which is fine, but it clearly wasn't fresh and it was barely warm. While I expect this in a mall, when I'm actually in a functioning restaurant I do have higher expectations. The pizza wasn't bad, but there's definitely no way I'd go out of my way for it. The pepperoni breadsticks were warm, though they lacked anything distinct in terms of flavor. I suppose for $7 it wasn't bad, but since I was splurging a bit on my diet I really was hoping for a tastier splurge. 

Bella's was semi-clean. It certainly wasn't divey, but I couldn't help but notice with 3-4 employees working and about as many customers that it seemed like socializing was a higher priority than actually cleaning or keeping busy. They weren't unfriendly and I didn't feel neglected, but with a little interaction with customers they could have really created a much more positive dining experience. 

With Indy really possessing a pretty good pizza scene these days, it's hard to fathom a good reason to return to Bella's. The employees didn't seem to care that I was there and, quite honestly, if you can't serve me a simple hot slice of pizza then you're really not worth my hard-earned dollars. With Napolese in the mall across the street and Puccini's not that far away, when I want a good meal I'll visit them and when I want mall pizza I'll actually go to the mall.
I got the best microdermabrasion at this med spa and their products were great too. I liked how the facialist gave me samples. I plan on being a regular here.
I've been here over a dozen times. The ice cream is ok, I really don't get the hoop-la over ice cream. And to be honest, I hate places that only accept cash.

Zero stars if I could! 

Don't waste your time or money on Remember Me.  The older lady who runs the place only runs clients away.  I had a bad experience the year before (the old lady was rude and breathing down my neck while looking for a costume), and dreaded to go into this place, but I lived right down the street and needed a costume quick.  I was on my cell while in a rush to grab and 80's outfit, talking to a friend who had been admitted to the hospital the night before.  There was only 1 other customer in the ENTIRE store other than myself.  

I wan't even allowed a chance to browse, she asked me exactly what I was looking for in a rude tone.  When I told her I was just going to browse, she loudly told me "NO".  She said No, I wasn't going to be in her store while I was on the phone, it was disturbing to all the other customers, that I would need to either get off the phone or leave if I wanted to talk on the phone.  I left immediately, extremely angry.

On my way to the mall to find an outfit (which I found something great at Forever 21 for VERY cheap), after getting off the phone with my friend I decided to call Miss Crabby pants from Remember Me to let her know her attitude wasn't necessary.  She didn't even allow me to finish what I was saying and hung up on me, twice!

This woman should not be allowed to run a business, especially a store that COULD be great.  There are some costumes that are really cute, but TRUST ME, it isn't worth it.
I'm not quite sure why this is grouped with "Best Black Owned Business" when it's not black-owned. Unless I am mistaken?

The boyfriend and I went to Samurai Sushi on a Friday night with high hopes as it is a place with 140 reviews that averaged 4 stars.  We learned that Nashville doesn't have a really great sushi restaurant to put bring this very average restaurant back down to earth.

We recently moved from Orlando so with our first paychecks we thought it'd be adorable to treat ourselves/celebrate new beginnings, etc etc etc.  6 rolls of sushi, a handful of sashimi, and about $70+ later, we were left with the overwhelming feeling of meeehhh.

Firstly, the fish isn't all that fresh and the rolls are over-done.  Whatever happened to just letting the integrity of the ingredients speak for itself?  It's freaking sushi. You don't need to put 10 different things into a roll and then deep fry it and then cover it in eel sauce for it to be delicious.  Some good quality fish and properly prepared rice is really all you need.  Let the quality of the fish be the star of the roll and for the love of god stop deep frying everything.  Generations of Japanese are rolling in their graves.  And what is with this whole strawberry sushi craze?  I thought I'd give it a shot based on Yelp recommendations and 2 weeks on, my stomach still churns at the memory.

It's not that Samurai is the absolute worst sushi in Nashville (you can go to Ken's for that), it's just that the food as a whole is really really mehhh.  I don't know if it's because TN has to source its fish from the coast and as a result all of its sushi restaurants suck or if its because Samurai just has a really cheap and therefore crappy fish supplier.  Either way, we wont' be back to Samurai.

Pros: 
1. the place is cheap.  3 "fancy" rolls, 3 normal rolls, about 8 pieces of sashimi, and 2 beers was about $75ish with tip.  
2. the restaurant is also cleaner than Ken's though that particular standard of cleanliness isn't really tough to beat.
3. most of the food isn't absolutely disgusting.

Cons:
1. the rolls consist of more ingredients than a Papa John's supreme pizza
2. the fish isn't really like that fresh.
3. overall just very average food.

Great atmosphere, great music, excellent food. One thing I will state is that this is not the place to come for fast service. Everyone works in relax no rush mode. But this is a great place if you looking have great food and simply look t relax and enjoy your surroundings!

Loving Indian dishes prepared by a couple who truly love what they do. Remembered me from several weeks ago and smiled warmly. Portions large enough to have lunch the next day with prices that won't break your wallet. Go here soon and tell your friends. We want them to stick around!

Everyone told me they had best cheesesteaks. I was skeptical but ordered pn with a salad. It was  delicous the bread was amazibg abd it wasnt soaked in grease. Salad was fresh and made perfect side. Defiantly recommend you try the cheesteak!

Butch did a great job. The tour was relaxing, informative but 2 good stops to eat and see the cemetery. I recommend going on this trip the beginning of your stay so you know where to go during your trip. He'a also pretty fun.

This was our first time at Le Peep. We loved it!  I had the Wanderer skillet, my wife had the Taco's duo, and my kids had the Plaincakes with chocolate chips.  Everything was awesome. Way better than I expected we'll be back for sure.

Went there for dinner with family and was not impressed what so ever. First of, the fish tank in the dining room is cool but not quite as grandiose as they make it seem. maybe I was spoiled going to Atlantis in Nassau. Regardless, the food is really overprice, the portion are ridiculous and the taste from plain to ok. My fiancee had the skewer which looked cool the way it was served but kinda ok taste, the kids shared pasta tortellini with shrimp and even they said it was the worse...and I had seafood bouillabaise, the worse I ever had. Overall felt completely ripped off. Our waitress was great and is not responsible for neither portion or taste coming out of this kitchen.

I went here with my boss a year ago. The food was delicious. Service was great. It was a little loud for our lunch but I would go back with friends. I tell many pilots(I work at an airport) to try it out for lunch and they have all loved it.

A great ballpark! There's never a bad view, no matter how high up your seats are. The best stadium food ever (except the beers are a little pricey). 

Always a fun time, even when the Phillies are playing horribly. The Phanatic really makes the game. It's always entertaining! A definite must go for spring/summer fun!

What a fun little find. Busy first thing in the morning! Our server was spunky and fun, just the right amount of perfect service. 

My husband was starving and grumpy after our red eye flight in from Cali, this was the perfect meal to perk him right up! 

I ordered plain crepes with powdered sugar, they were thick unlike an ordinary crepe which was a little weird but, none the less delicious. I topped them off with some cinnamon-cream syrup. My husband enjoyed a meaty man omelet with a side of cinnamon and sugar pancakes. 

The portions are just right. Totally worth the extra 10 min drive from the airport.
the worst restaurant  experience. we were ignored by the waitress

I've never had this kind of food and I was in the mood to try something different and healthier. I wasn't disappointed. As I read other reviews I saw many good things about the don don noodles so I decided to give it a try.  The noodles had a weird texture to it but I'm pretty sure it was the spices on it. It was delicious and the little pieces of pork made it that much better tasting.

Came here for brunch with family and friends and we really enjoyed our meals. I had the chicken and waffles and it was decent. Looks like I missed out and should have order the burger instead because that tasted awesome. Cool atmosphere and nice service. Definitely will return to try their dinner menu!

This is a review of the Ramble Pizza food truck when it's been at the Mt. Airy Weavers Way Co-op location on Fridays. A great addition to the neighborhood. Happily, they sell pizza by the slice. I've only tried the mushroom pizza and plain cheese pizzas. Cheeses were very good, and some of you might prefer an even thinner crust "Roman" style, so this was pizza in the thicker end of the Roman style spectrum. Nevertheless excellent - what is better than a pizza right out of the oven? I had some concerns about how they'd turn out a pizza from an oven in a food truck, but was very pleased with the results. Owner-run and operated, and they are really friendly, nice people.

Service: Great. 

Burger: Perfect. I rate the burger at 8.5 which is pretty high for me (Higher than Shake Shack & Five Guys). The best in St Louis so far. 

Atmosphere: awesome if u like pop music. Good design. Decent place. 

Price: worth it. 

I'd definitely come back.

I would say A-Ok for the Towneplace Suites.   Ok...but not the best Marriott we have stayed at.   The beds were comfortable.   Our room was cleaned well.   The breakfast could be a bit better.  One morning they ran out of spoons.   The bacon looked funny... almost like it wasn't real bacon.   They were constantly running around trying to replenish something it was eggs or sausage or milk.  It just seemed a bit disorganized.   We would choose another place to stay if we visit again.   I can't be really negative, but I can't highly recommend this place either.  This is a very conflicted review.

Don't eat here! Worse dining experience I had in NOLA. To begin with, they're severely understaffed. This resulted in not only a long wait to order and be served your food at their lil bar stools, but also the food was cold. I had the jambalaya, which tasted like it was straight out of a Zatarran's box, which is fine if you weren't paying $10 for it. My mom had the grilled shrimp poboy. Much to her dismay the shrimp was not grilled and it was not large shrimp, but rather small baby shrimp. We never got a refill on our diet coke nor were we given water. Whatever you do, don't waste your money here at this tourist trap. There are plenty of other eateries to experience local fare

The first time I went here I was in college and my friend and I had this ridiculously hilarious obsession (it started as joke and just snowballed) about Chili's El Presidente margaritas. Neither of us are crazy about Chili's food (what is there to be crazy about) we only went there for the margaritas. 

Yes, that is kind of a weird thing to do, but they were so damn good. 

I think we went there twice to have their El Presidente margaritas then we decided that it might taste better if we could eliminate Chili's from the equation. 

Anyway, somehow my friend figured out what the ingredients were, either by asking the bartender or just watching one being made. It had, among other things, cointreau, which is not hard to find but it also had some kind of tequila I cannot remember the name of that was like the unicorn of tequilas. 

I kid you not my friend and I were calling liquor stores all over to see if they had this tequila that we needed because we wanted the recipe to be 100% exactly like what is served at the restaurant. 

We called and called and it seemed like the dream of an El Presidente margarita minus the whole being at Chilli's thing was slipping away. But we kept trying, damn it we knew someone would have it.

Guess where we found it? Dorignac's. 

Their alcohol selection is the bee's knees. I am pretty sure they have bottles of vodka the size of my vacuum cleaner. 

I have not done any regular grocery shopping here which makes me sound like a saucy boozehound. 

For me it comes down to what I need and convenience, this place is just a little far away for me to be doing general grocery shopping. I will, however, l take a look around their meat department and deli next time I am there. It is a really unique store and from what I have heard I imagine they stock a lot of high quality products.

i really wanted to like fairwheel bikes, primarily because they're extremely convenient--between where i park and where i work on campus. they carry brands i like and they look like the type of bike store i used to frequent when i lived in oregon.
i had one favorable experience where they fixed the seal on my silca pump and were friendly and expedient, but my other experiences have been pretty shoddy. my other experiences have been as if the mechanics and salesmen were "too cool for school." i was treated as if i didn't know anything and when i brought my wheels in to have the cassette swapped the guy backed my rear wheel out of the bracket so far it kept falling out. then he proceded to patronize me for several minutes.
i may go back if i need a tube or to look for a take-off saddle, but otherwise i won't be spending any siginificant money with them, much less let them service my sweet old steelie.

I love the food here! The Reubens are awesome..the burgers as well. The pizza is my favorite. No matter what topping you get, the crust stands up to it. Terrific beer selection. I definitely will be back

We've just had dinner at Eatalia for the 2nd time in the last 3 months and each time, our meal has been delicious.  The quality and consistency of the cooking and the creative daily specials really makes this place a true "find", in my opinion.  

Just a few minutes off I-95, it's easier to get here than to most restaurants in Center City or South Philly and the free street parking couldn't be any easier.  Overall, this is a comfortable, reasonably priced, unassuming neighborhood BYOB which has become one of my new favorites.

New traditional Mexican food from Ventura. We used to live on Ventura ave where the original one is and it was our favorite and we were SO sad to leave it when we moved to SB. This new location has changed our lives!!

The al Pastor meat is to die for and the tacos are amazing. They have such good tortas (cubana) and Alambres (plates with tortillas on the side). The price is right on and the salsa bar is so good. 

The owners are the nicest people and they made a big leap coming up here so support them and their amazing food!!

This place is absolutely the best kept secret in Delco! Great authentic Italian food with amazing service. The wait staff seems to be all from Italy and the owner is super nice guy! I have loved everything Ive tried but the veal is my favorite.

I am staying at the Grand Sierra Resort in Reno and went to look for lunch.  I was in the mood  for a burger so Johnny Rockets appeared to fit the bill.  This was my first visit to this chain.  I am skeptical about any chain but this was a wonderful surprise.   They were very busy but we were greeted by an energetic waitress named Lyndel.  She was amazing.  We felt like we were the only customers in the place.  After a few jokes and a smile she took our order.  The food came quickly and as perfectly prepared.  The portions were large.  The burgers, fries and milkshake were all better than any chain I had been to.  In the end it was a very good experience.  My hat is off to Lyndel for doing a job so well that it makes a lunch like this memorable.

Took my vehicle here for some work a few years ago for a manufacturer recall. Problem went away and then started hearing another noise which I thought was related, but turned out was a completely different issue. Kevin and his mechanic lifted my car right up and fixed the issue FREE OF CHARGE even though I told them I'd pay. Outstanding individuals for doing that. Highly recommend!

Small kitchen experience with an intimate dining feel. Trendy and engaging. The server recommended a drink off the menu for my taste and the mixologist served it up.right. wings for appetizers., sliders and.pork chop for dinner. A great night out!

I came here for a industry/networking event but have to say I was very impressed with their coffee.     After an experience in a 'gourmet' coffee shop you start to realize that Starbucks is the McDonalds of coffee - you're going to get the same tasting stuff and the same experience no matter where you go.

The store has a nice vibe and while the location is slightly off the beaten path for many it works well.    The inside of the store is clean and bright with plenty of seating (there is also a large lounge area).    They offer several different options for milk (Regular milk, soy milk and almond milk) as well as every flavored syrup you could ask for including stuff I'd never heard before.  I ended up having a vanilla-orange soy latte that tasted absolutely fantastic.

They do the foam art which is pretty cool too, it's less dramatic if you're having soy milk but nice never the less.  All the staff was courteous and friendly too.   I'll definitely be back to Swill to try more drinks!

Mmm teriyaki burger is the best! I have tried the other burgers and they are delicious as well. Highly recommend if you're a In n Out regular. Although both are very different you'll soon become a habit regular!

Food is decent. Slow but ok service. Asked to watch a golf tournament on one of the TVs and it took them 45 mins to change the channel (asked 3 times). We would have stayed longer and had more drinks etc if anyone bothered to accommodate paying customers.

Not bad for a first visit! I ordered the Farmhouse Breakfast, which includes eggs your way, two slices of bacon, potatoes and choice of toast. For a Saturday brunch we were in and out in an hour but when we left it was getting busy so don't be surprised if there is a wait.

Bub's Burgers down the street starts every meal with a free chili shooter, and Bub's Cafe version is a small container of granola - yum. 

I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here but it is a convenient breakfast in the Carmel Arts & Design District.

While the portions are generous the quality of the food is NOT! I tried the fried chicken and was underwhelmed. It was under-seasoned and flavorless much like accompanying sides of coleslaw, baked beans and sweet potato fries. Given the location there are countless restaurants of higher quality and value within a few miles distance. The resturaunt was clean and the service was average but there was a bizarre moment when the waiter/host stopped helping customers and  began performing live music. I know it's Nashville and being the home of country music is kind of the shtick, but it was a fail. The guy was pretty terrible and began by asking for requests from customers but didn't know any of the requested songs. Instead, he sang some "originals" that reinforced my two star rating. 

My advice... Catch a taxi or drive downtown and enjoy the real Nashville atmosphere and cuisine this place is trying to reproduce.

This review was written by one of my students:
I would go to Gamestop when I need to buy games and to search for games. There are a lot of games in stands and cases on the walls and floors. I usually have to ask for help finding the game I want and sometimes they are busy and I have to wait or don't get help.  When they have time, they open the cases so I can choose different games. The staff is not rude. Sometimes they are friendly.  Sometimes the game consoles are really expensive and also the controllers that go with them. Some games are less expensive - about $30 per game. I always want to go back to GameStop for my games.  I do need a ride there because it is far from my house.  4 star rating.

Hammy isn't too sure about this place--lots of dark lights and loud music. I tripped and fell. Also, the bartender made my whiskey and coke with vodka and soda. Something's amiss with the restrooms as well. Talk to you soon. Hammy rules!!!

Moving into our new house and I think the Italian hoagie saved my life. Happy to be living close.

Just ate lunch from there again today. 2 days in a row!

I  drove  by  this  restaurant  last  night.  What  a  fun ,  brightly  lit  neighborhood.  I  hope  to  return  and  eat  here.  Looks  like  Florida  has  some  great  new  nightlife.
Hidden  somewhere  between  Ybor  City  and  downtown  Tampa....

One of my favorite places to take people when they come to town.  Unique place tucked away on a side street in Society hill, the food is good, cheap and just keeps coming.  The second "dish" is my favorite, but lets be real anything with powdered sugar is amazing.  It's $70 for two people, which includes tax and tip.  It's BYOB, but you can also buy booze there is you want.  I don't love the belly dancers roaming the restaurant, but I am sure I am in the minority there.  

If you have a chance, definitely worth a trip.  Just remember, it's cash only.

I am so sad to see this place is closed. Circa 2009 my wife and I were there three days staying just down the street and ate there for breakfast on the second and third mornings - and wished we'd found it the first morning and we would have made it a triple.

My wife loved whatever she ate enough to want to return and I had the crayfish benedict both mornings. I have ever since called it the best breakfast I've ever had and I have long wanted to return just to eat there again. 

The place was charming and it seemed like a hidden find/treasure (which, if true, might not be the best for keeping busy).

Alas, I guess I'll have to settle for my second best breakfast, eggs bennedict at http://www.yelp.com/biz/sneakers-bistro-and-cafe-winooski?
Had some for a building holiday party. Very good food. Meatballs and sweet potato's were delicious

Okay, we were off to a bad start.  Party of 9 (4 adults & 5 kids ages 8-12).  It wasn't packed ( but we were packed in a kind of wrap around booth).  

We were there an hour before our food was served.  The waitress kept up with drink refills and apologies.  5-stars for her!

When the food finally arrived it was hot and impressive in both taste and presentation.  The burgers were mile-high with toppings, and the kids meals satisfied our big kids. I would say worth the wait but that wait was way too long with no visit from the management.   

I'll come back for the Cowboy Burger and hope for the best.

I finally bought something here and It was definitely a pleasant experience.

A few years ago I stopped in here with friend who was buying film. I asked one of the salesman about a problem I was having with my camcorder. Even though I wasn't there to buy anything for myself, he still spent some time to help me out and gave me info on where to send my camcorder to get fixed by Canon. That is when I knew I'd be back to Schiller's if I ever wanted to buy a new camera. 

Last week I stopped in to see what my options were. A fellow named Brad asked me if I needed help. He was very helpful and patient with me. He answered all of my questions and helped me narrow down the selection. There were three that I was interested in so he wrote the brand and models down on his business card. He probably expected that I would buy one for cheaper on the internet but that was out of the question. I did some research on the cameras and decided on one of them. 

A few days later I returned but Brad was busy with another customer. Some other gentlemen that worked there helped me out until Brad was done with the other customer. The camera I purchased was about $60 more at Schiller's than on the internet but the customer service was totally worth it for me. The extra battery and memory card put the price a bit above what I wanted to spend but then Brad told me since I bought the camera there, I get 25 free prints every month for a year. That was totally worth spending the extra dough on an extra battery and then he even threw in a little camera case! What a guy! 

Schiller's seems to have a great selection of cameras and camera equipment. The one gentleman that helped me for a minute was a little awkward to deal with and my friend said he had a little bit of difficulty with customer service. Brad and the guy who helped me with my camcorder were great to deal with so I guess it all depends on which employee is helping you. I definitely recommend giving Schiller's a chance. I'm a huge fan of supporting local businesses, even if you are dead set on buying from a big chain store or on the internet, at least stop in and see what they have and what there prices are.

Where to begin, a $ 7 tip was added to my bill prior to Svc rendered. Shouldn't that be my choice. It is a gratuity is it not? My order took over 2 hours to arrive. When the gentleman arrived he did apologize for the delay. The reason I have never heard before. He told me a coworker took his car to p/u his/her daughter from school. That's a new one. So as you see, 2 hour delay does not = a $7 gratuity, nor does it = more than 1 star.

Great atmosphere as soon as you walk in, we were taken to our table very quickly. I will leave this brief because to be honest the food tasted fine, but I wasn't THAT impressed. PROS: the delicious French Onion soup. CONS: I guess my main concern was the itty bitty crab cakes I ordered. Paying the price that I did for that small of an order of crab cakes is RIDICULOUS. At the Chophouse in Charleston, for that price I received a crab cake the size of my face! Someone in the group ordered a filet that wasn't cooked to medium perfection. The sea bass my friend ordered looked pretty good, but I tasted his au gratin potatoes and they were  completely underwhelming. My friend also ordered the Chicken Piccata which tasted fine. Managed to snag a last minute reservation for SIX on a Saturday... and now I now why.  The ambiance is nice, and the food tasted okay, but I would not eat here again.

My boyfriend and I finally ate here last night after wanting to visit for awhile. 

FOOD
All of their dinner entrees range from about $16-$28, making this an upscale Mexican restaurant. They aim to be very authentic with details such as: making all of their own sauces, having only Mexican beers, etc. They have delicious salsa here and give you endless chips before your meal - yay! I had the mixto flat iron tacos and my boyfriend had chicken enchiladas. My tacos were delicious! They come fajita-style, meaning you make your own tacos. The cheese that the meat came in was delicious. It would be cool if they found a way to keep the cheese soft, as it sort of seized up after a bit. That being said, I eat relatively slowly. My boyfriend's enchiladas looked amazing and he loved them! Everything was wonderful. 

SERVICE
Service was awesome! Our server was kind, knowledgeable, and checked on us frequently. He made the restaurant that much better! We haven't had that good of service in a long time. They end every meal with churros (so good) and worry dolls. It's such a nice touch. 

ATMOSPHERE 
This place is beautiful and busy! We ate on the covered patio and it was lovely. They have pretty lights hanging everywhere and it doesn't get too loud. The inside of the restaurant looked beautiful as well. Everything was decorated well. 

We will definitely be back and had a great time here!

I really, REALLY love the Reuben and the salads. The meat is sliced thin and not fatty on the Reuben and possibly steamed before frying the sandwich? It's probably my favorite Reuben in town. Salads just feel like a fresh garden. Tasty and they aren't stingy on all the components. 

Service though, as others have noted, is not always the best. I get that they're busy at lunch but the last time I went in for something to go (which was ready in decent time, no complaints there) I was given the wrong salad for my "you choose two" order and on another occasion I didn't get dressing on my salad takeout order. 

Delicious food, a little lacking on attention to detail sometimes during busy hours.

This place is amazing.  They offer a lot.of alternative breads from flours like spelt flour.  They also have delicious pesto spinach buns. I also recommend the spelt flour buns, they are great for a healthier option sandwich or hamburger.
I just expect more from a Wawa. It's not that it was bad, but the fact that I waited for almost 20 minutes for a latte is ridiculous, no matter how late at night it is.

Myself and my son went here on the rare Saturday night that I had off from work. I had a giant margarita, and we both had the steaks. I always love this location, it's never really crazy and loud like some of the other locations and the staff are always very friendly. Plus it's good for a 9 year old, which makes a difference to us!

After a horrendous stay at the La Quinta airport in Nashville we stayed at this lovely place. Staff are soooo sweet and customer oriented.. Kathy at desk and the young black man and woman in the evening are GREAT...SO SWEET AND HELPFUL..good breakfast, comfortable room..only negatives are they need more seating areas for breakfast and need to service the fitness facility with towels, cleaning and empty trash. We will be staying here again. Thanks to the wo derful desk staff.. Breakfast staff were also exceptionally good.

They are just perfect for what I want. Second visit for me and again nothing went wrong. If you just want to have fresh Crawfish, shrimp or oysters... come visit here. I had a dozen each of freshly shucked oyster in front of you and fried oyster!!! My my my..... the room is not clean, table is rough set up and people work here are like buddies; thus, you'll love it here:)))) Will be back 350%~!

Comfort Food in a comfortable setting.  This is sort of like a more interesting version of a hometown diner; the kind of place where friendly people from the community meet and eat BUT where the food ranges from great cheeseseaks to homemade pasta, grilled veggies and Asian delicacies.  The specials are always changing and so creative and tasty. I never order off the menu and usually ask Misha, the delightful owner/chef,  to make me whatever she likes. It is always a wonderful surprise. Try the homemade dumplings for lunch. For breakfast, pancakes are the best around. Call ahead to order if you are in a rush. This place is busy; especially around lunchtime.  Or take it outside and sit at the tables on the sidewalk for a moving portrait of small town Americana.

This place is one of a kind. All hand-painted, hand-drawn letters. They make custom signs here (the portfolio shows signs all over New Orleans), and there's also a TON of stuff in the front part of the shop, with small signs, prints, posters and other art/jewelry for sale. They also sometimes teach various lettering classes in the evenings. 

I go here frequently and absolutely love it. For the record, I had to inquire about the one bad review, and Eve's side of the story is quite different. No need to get into details here, but I don't think it's fair that one person on an emotional internet tirade can have such an impact on a Yelp rating. So here's my two cents - five stars all the way.
Love the mojo pork! Cafe Con Leche on Saturday morning is the best with cheese toast.

I really wanted to like this place and I'm feeling sad. 

Made reservations for birthday dinner. Everyone was very friendly, great service and ambience... At first. 

We ordered a bottle of wine and 2 appetizers the Fritto Misto and the Burrata. I wanted to take my time, have some wine and try the food before I selected an entree. The appetizers were underwhelming to say the least. They were fine, we ate them... But I really wasn't impressed.  Nothing seemed fresh, and I was beginning to have a bad feeling about ordering an entree. 

Instead my guy ordered an entree and I got a salad and I'm so glad I did. He ordered the Cioppino and it just wasn't good. It wasn't warm enough, the broth had no flavor, and the seafood wasn't right. I HATE sending things back but it really wasn't good. The server said he would talk to the "owner" to see what could be done. They offered to replace it with another entree. I'm sorry but after two apps, a salad and an entree all being sub-par, I don't want to waste any more of your food or my time. 

Maybe we ordered the wrong things, or that was just an off dish. The problem came when for the rest of the meal we got sideways looks from the staff and the server gave us forced apologies. I even apologized and explained that we did not want to be insulting but genuinely did not enjoy the food.  They didn't charge us for the entree, which was appreciated. But we still spent over $100, left hungry, and on my birthday I felt like an inconvenience instead of a guest. 

We like to spend money on food... Just not mediocre food. We went somewhere else and had excellent food for less.

This was going to be a five star review. After all, who am I to break a streak? BUT, it was not to be. After finding this particular Meineke online via Yelp (yay), I trusted enough to send my wife with the car to get an oil change. I found ON MEINEKE.COM the full synthetic package for 69.95, including hinge such as tire rotation for no extra charge! I was like, WHAT?!?!?!?!? Most non-jifflubey shops charge 80-90 for the oil and filter and then try to upcharge for everything else. Again, I was impressed, so I made the appointment and sent the wifey on her merry way while I was at work. (cut to the appointment) The wife texts me, says the shop looks like crap outside, but once you get inside, it's a whole different ballgame. She meets with who I can only assume is the service writer, who seats her and heads off on his way (at this point, there has been no talk of anything beyond the service requested by me online). They quote the wife about 45 minutes and get to work. About 30 minutes or so later, here comes the up-sell attempt. They want to change the brake fluid on a nearly new (2016) SUV with just over 20,000 miles on it. She texts me, I scoff. The end? Au contraire. They also want to do a rotate and balance for $40 bucks. Um. Rotate is included according to the website, not so, says the SW, trying to pad that margin. "We used to do specials like that, but not anymore" he says. Uh huh. Ok, so I say do it and I'll handle it later when I get home. The wife (whose raving about how nice and non-pressury and "humble" the techs and SW were is the ONLY reason they got three stars) was happy, so We're three star happy. I really wish I could have gone five, but they ruined it. To repost my blurb from FB and the Twit,

Hey @MeinekeCarCare? FYI, you may want to either take down your "old, incorrect" advertising, or tell your franchisee techs to stand by your offers. Paid $111 for this today after I was told Meineke didn't offer it anymore:


----UPDATE 17APR18----
So John reached out to me today, and fully explained how and why he does what he does, and it made perfect sense. Bumping up to 5 stars, one for the fact that he actually reached out (something a LOT of shop owners fail to do), and he second because what he does makes perfect sense, not just from a business standpoint, but from a consumer standpoint.

Keep up the great work, John! You'll definitely be seeing me (or my wife) again!

First time here, excited to try the place as another new restaurant in the area.  It's a cool looking interior, very open planned & great use of space.  

While waiting for our table, grabbed a quick drink at the bar, took over 15 minutes to be served, even when took our order continued to serve others before got our drink.  When got to the table, on the edge of the restaurant, with one of us facing the wall, quickly realized that we weren't going to be treated as a large number of the other customers.  There were 3 front of house/ managers floating between the tables checking out certain select customers, blatantly demonstrating that only a few customers were worth paying attention to.

To be fair our waiter was great, attentive & making sure we had everything we needed.  Only criticism for him was around not serving the lady first, but that seems to be the case in nearly all restaurants these days!

The food was ok, disappointing that we had not finished our starter before the main came to the table, our waiter apologized, but didn't feel like had much choice as would have gone back under the lights until we were ready!

I get it, it's the Main Line, what do you expect, but we've eaten in a ton of restaurants in Philly including all the top ones & have never seen this kind of pretentiousness before!

Super greasy pizza which usually I don't mind but it was salty and greasy! I wanted to order their special 2 slices for 4.99 but they did not have any slices so my only choice was to order a whole pizza for just me. I also purchased tiramisu (my absolute favorite dessert that usually no one can mess up) but it was freezer burnt and hard!?!  I usually always enjoy trying mom and pop pizza places at places I visit on travel but this one is definitely one I would not go to again!  I should've driven the extra 10minutes and found a better spot!  Lesson learned!
Affordable and delicious! I haven't ordered something that I didn't  like. Grab a bottle of wine and enjoy a great meal. Portions are good too.

I go to Marmont as often as I can, the food is amazing every time and the prices are reasonable as well. I always get the filet and Marmont salad and am never disappointed! 
I love the atmosphere, it's not too loud during dinner hours and especially in the spring/summer season when diners are able to sit outside and enjoy all of what Olde City has to offer! 
The service is impeccable and their drink menu, especially all of their martinis, are to die for! It's great for dates to grab dinner and afterwards hang out for drinks and the dining room turns into a dance floor with a DJ. 
Marmont is by far one of my favorite places to go to in Philadelphia whenever I'm in the city!
Got here as they were getting ready to close down - needed a caffeine pick me up before the long walk back to the hotel. The orchata cappuccino did not disappoint. Pricy, but tasty.
This place has the best pho and spring rolls I've had in my life and on top of that the service was amazing.

Not just for feet. All I can say is....Wow! Worth the extra $$ for an hour full body massage. Simon has the most talented hands to coax your muscles to relax, taking the kinks out with skill. The atmosphere is very desirable and comfortable. You don't realized the importance of human touch until you have a professional work their magic. They provide walk-in service, but I recommend scheduling an appointment for a massage, especially during the early evening hours. My daughter and I had a foot massage there and this too was fantastic! First place whose prices are affordable and well worth indulging in. I highly recommend this little slice of heaven.

My Office Home away from Office Home lol....Thank goodness I found one because Kmart, Wal-Mart,  Target etc... were all out of needed school folders that schools give you a list for and you have to go on a huge treasure hunt with other frantic parents to find.  Hmmm...you know what I mean.  Worth every penny @$1.49 a folder.  Staff there was cool, stock guy even gave me the folders right off the cart he was unloading from.

First time here, was recommended by some friends. The place was pretty busy when we when on a Monday night which was a good sign.
We were greeted promptly and seated,a server took a drink order right away, another good sign.
They brought out garlic rolls, another good sign.
We ordered different pastas and baked clams, all very good.
This is not a high end place, it's a good neighborhood spot if you're in the mood for Italian and don't want to spend a fortune.
We will return and next time see what the desert menu looks like.

The owner is super nice and friendly. Great customer service. 

I came here for a few yoga classes, but what I really want to recommend are the massages! Specifically for Shea! She was so amazing, and kind. I was a very stressed out graduate student, with a lot of tension in my back from studying. After 1 massage with her, I had never felt so relaxed in my life. Life changing really. I actually fell asleep a few times during the massage. She has the most healing touch. I also kept dozing off throughout the day afterwards - I was that relaxed! Head to toe relaxation.

Her set up is very clean. I like things to be quiet during a massage, and she respected that :)

I bought a pkg of massages, and was very sad when I used my last one up. I have had many massages since them, high end joints in Center City, as far away as high end resorts in Phuket, Thailand, and I must say I still always think of Shea and coming back to Experience Yoga. 

Only small con, the massage room is in a back room that is separated from a rear exit by a screen. One time someone left through there, and it was a bit distracting.

We stumbled onto this restaurant after seeing the very long line at Hattie B's. The atmosphere seemed really nice and the wait for a table much more manageable-only 10 minutes. The menu choices were appealing and we put in an order for two burgers, fries, a fish sandwich and trail salad.  Then we waited, and waited and waited some more.  Fifty minutes later our food still did not arrive with no real explanation (or apology) from our server.  The manager was pleasant and after she was alerted our food did arrive. The burgers were tasty as were the Belgian fries. The trail mix salad had too many dried cranberries for my liking making it much too sweet.  I think with a different server the experience may have been more positive, but with so many great restaurants in Nashville I won't be going back to find out.

Great breakfast! Service was wonderful and met one of the "chicks". She was delightful to talk to and hear about the restaurant. I had a buckwheat crepe with crab, shrimp and veggies. Topped with an egg! Definitely see the Romanian influence. My wife had French toast and loved it.

Love their chicken strips! I have only ordered takeout, so I can't comment on the atmosphere much, but the strips and fries are delicious. Nice crispy chicken, always ready on time. $15 for a 6 piece, but it's enough to feed both me and my husband. 

They will only include sauce if you ask for it. Their signature is a sweet and hot sauce. Its good!

The parking can be a little tricky since it is in a residential area, the space is a little cramped, but the  best chicken you will find outside of your own kitchen. I also like the potato salad and greens beans

I am a little late in my review, but I attended their media event/grand opening for the unveiling of their "Legends Wall" which proudly showcases sports legends such as Lee Roy Selmon, Ronde Barber, Eddie DeBartolo and more. I sampled many of their signature items and was extremely impressed with the service I received at the bar. The bar staff is awesome and attentive. The entire place is beautiful and if I lived closer, I would be a regular. Food is delicious and I left deliriously happy.  My night ended on a sweet note with having the opportunity to meet Ronde himself.  He was super kind and took time to sign autographs. If you are looking for an upscale casual sports bar in Carrollwood, look no further.

If zero stars was an option I would choose that!  

The doctor here LIED and told my wife and I that our current contact lens brand was discontinued.  It was not discontinued he just wanted to push a newer, "better" version on us which we both told him we did not like after we had tried it.  So after suffering through these awful, and more expensive lenses for over a year we did our research and realized we should have caught this from the beginning and left then.  Shame on us, but I hope this can save someone from the same mistake.

When I called the office to request my current and old prescription numbers so we could make a switch the receptionist was extremely rude.  She then proceeded to tell me that I had made a decision to change contact brands.  I laughed and then explained that in reality the Dr. had lied in order to forced me into this decision, and furthermore I really disliked the way I was being spoken to and simply wanted to get my prescriptions so that we never had to speak again.  I believe she understood at this point and shut up.

I would never recommend anyone to this office.

Laura has been doing my hair for years. I've tried other stylists in times when I couldn't make an appointment but I've always come back to Laura. She has created a custom cut and color for me and I always get compliments on it everywhere. She KNOWS hair and cuts very well and will give her honest and professional opinion when it comes to a different style. Whenever I ask about a particular style she will let me know how to look my best.

She runs a great, inviting business. Recently she has redecorated the salon and give nit a much more open and inviting feel. 

Prices are very reasonable for the amazing service and finished look. She also sells Aveda make up and skin products.

Gizmo ' s is your typical resale booth mall that rents booth space to individuals. Gizmo's Mall doesn't seem to have as much turn-over as other mall locations. Spaces consist of used clothing, including wedding and prom dresses, jewlery, all types of home decor and collectables, vintage glassware, coin collections and antique furniture. A few booths focus on the renter's own craft projects of floral arrangements, homemade soaps, candles, aprons, wreathes, woodworking pieces and refurbished furniture. Most have a theme or similarity within their booth space but you'll run across a few that are just a hodgepodge of random items. The majority of booths are fairly well organized and clean but again, a couple have dropped the ball. If available, an employee tries to walk around checking on customers and takes any items you are carrying to the front for you. They place your items in one of the hold baskets until you're ready to check out.

I'm usually on a mission searching for something fairly specific when I shop here. Occasionally I walk out without anything and other times I stumble across a great deal or unique find. The prices obviously vary greatly from booth to booth but are comparable to other booth malls. 

The folks working at the counter are super friendly and helpful. One thing I'd love to see is decluttering of the counter tops. It's getting harder and harder to find space to even sit your purse down to pay much less place your items.

Worth a trip if you're in the area. With holidays starting everyone will step up their game and restocking booths often with new items. Grab it when you see it because the holidays get hectic.

We came here based off a recommendation from our hotel.  The food was fine but nothing impressive.  It was basic bar food.  The music was way too loud.  Impossible to have a conversation and we were there at 5:30 on a Saturday.  If you're in from out of town, try another place for dinner.

My experience with this truck is mixed.  Veg couscous seemed healthy but was pretty bland. Smoked salmon sandwich (with egg, radish, caviar) was great.

Service can be very slow at times -- sometimes he chats for extended periods with certain people.

Place milked my tits entirely dry. I don't think I've ever been milked this hard from a coffee establishment. Starbucks has absolutely nothing on Milktooth. All the treats look incredible especially the pecan sticky bun. The pictures in the bano are stellar, just a bunch of race car drivers gettin after it livng their best leche lives.
Really nice place to get a pedicure! People are very friendly and it is a relaxing environment. Definitely recommend if you are looking for a clean place to get your toes done!

I have to agree with most of the previous reviewers.  It's unremarkable - literally.  There isn't much to say about it.  There isn't anything to commend nor anything to chastise.  

It's on my walk home so I go in when I'm craving some Chinese.  I've tried others in the area but this is probably the best.  Sadly, the Chinese food scene in University City is kind of lame.
Food is always good. Service is fast.   Love the location and owners are friendly. Come here weekly.

The bar and staff are AMAZING. we got a room upgrade for have been being on our honeymoon and the view was gorgeous. But, the room was not any better than a hilton. It had rust in the tub floor, and some weird stains on the tile. But this was only in the bathroom, so i give it 4 stars! Great staff, but too much for valet so we parked a couple streets down. That was the only other con I would say. 

Would recommend if you want to be literally in the working downtown area of st. louis. Lots of cool bars and restaurants on a friday night.
Best thai food in the area.  Everything was authentic and delicious.  Will definitely be back again and again.

We stayed at the Four Points for 3 nights in November, while here on business.  Nice hotel, and a good experience. 

Check in was a breeze.  We had a good price on the room via my Sheraton/SPG member and AAA discount, which included the free breakfast.  The hotel is literally 5 minutes from the airport, and there are several other hotels right on the same block.

Staff was friendly and helpful.  Room was fine, parking easy, quiet at night.

I am surprised the average rating is 3.5 stars. For what it is, a soccer bar, I think this place is great and I actually prefer this location to the Mass Ave one.

The decor makes you feel like you're at an English pub. There are TVs everywhere so it's a great place to watch a game.

The beer selection is great, the service is great and the food is good. I've had their chicken salad sandwich, wings and fish and chips and all three are good. Better than your typical bar food.

The best apple cider donuts I have ever had! These are hands down my favorite and I have been coming here since I was a kid. Now this place has changed radically since then as it used to be an actual orchard with pick your own apples and pumpkins and hayrides, but the donuts at least have not changed. Where other apple cider donuts are heavy and greasy, these are light and airy. When you get them right out of the fryer and the cinnamon and sugar is on yours hands, perfection. 

They also do all you can eat nights and brunch. I have been to the pasta night on Thursdays, and it is a good bargain for your money, but it is not going to be the best pasta you have ever eaten. It is more of a get what you pay for situation. Again the same experience with brunch. It is consistently good food, but it isn't going to blow you away. Except the donut french toast is pretty neat. They cut the donut in half and cook it like it's french toast. That is pretty great. 

This place is also a BYOB which is always great. They have this one room upstairs which is hung with lights and branches and looks like a pinterest-worthy area to have a lady's brunch. Something I may have to convince my friends to try.

My boyfriend and I stayed in the "Deluxe King + Whirlpool Tub" room last year in May. It was a great experience! The Eagle Inn is clean, pretty and so comfortable. I don't think the prices are too bad considering I love it so much...however, if any of you are questioning whether you should stay here because of the cost, say YES and book it! The little extra cost can actually save you money if you take advantage of the breakfast provided (and it's great)! I agree with other reviewers that the staff is great, helpful and friendly without being overly ecstatic ("annoying") like other popular chain hotels. I can see this place being good for everyone....families, couples and friends. I'll be back in about 10 days and I cannot wait to relax in the peaceful atmosphere of the Eagle Inn.

Barrio Brewing Co. had some good, house-made brews (I had a nice IPA and my dining companions enjoyed the wheat beer and Scotch ale) but that's about it. The menu was mostly nothing-special bar food. My "Fire Starter" burger had some nice flavor with all the chilies but other burgers just looked greasey. The place is off the beaten path in an industrial section of Tucson. It was fun to watch the trains go by. Not a lot of air conditioning when I was there and the service was mediocre. I would recommend you try this place with a group of friends just to enjoy the weird industrial ambiance.
Food was great but the service was absolutely unacceptable.  Waitress was a mess and took 45 min to get our check right.

My wife and I visit New Orleans regularly, and every time we're there, we go to Lüke every day for Happy Hour. Their oysters are stellar, and at half price, I eat four dozen at a sitting. We have tried quite a few of the items on their menu, and my wife recently had their Ragout of Wild Boar and loved it. I tried it too, and it was a fantastic treat. Their Crab Bisque rocks, and it's a decent sized portion. We've also had the Flamenkuchen, which is like a flatbread pizza with bacon and onion; it's quite tasty and crispy. We've had their giant Lüke burgers and loved them too, they're fantastic, and prepared perfectly. In fact, we brought their burgers back on the plane last year, and they were delectable. They serve a bevy of beers, whiskeys, cognacs, wines and other spirits, all of high quality and drinkability. I actually drink the Mountain Valley Sparkling Water most of the time, with an occasional beer or wine, which are also half price for Happy Hour. The servers here are great, and we drew one of the same friendly waiters, Kyle P., that we had last year, for a couple of our visits this year. He was exceptional and warm, as well as genuine. The service is fast,  but not rushed, and the manner is warm and professional. The atmosphere is upscale, but not pretentious or haughty, and the dress is from business, to t-shirt-casual. The prices are not cheap, but the food is outstanding. Owner John Besh runs a tight ship, and we owe our lovely friend Marci for turning us on to their Happy Hour. Thank you Lüke for making our afternoons between 3 and 6pm in New Orleans, oyster-packed, comfort-food-filled and very enjoyable.

Our dog Sadie just finished up all three levels of training with Debbi at PetSmart, and passed her CGC exam! Sadie is a VERY energetic dog, and we've BOTH learned so much from spending our Tuesday nights with Debbie over the last 10 months. She genuinely cares so much about the dogs in these classes, and will take the time to work with you on the things she knows your dog is capable of doing and learning. Sadie nearly jumps through the car window any time we drive into the parking lot for class, because she is so happy to see Debbi and her dog class friends. There truly aren't enough good things that I can say about Debbi - she is amazing and I feel like we hit the jackpot by finding her training classes. PetSmart is very lucky to have her!

I'm a big fan of St Louis Bread Co, but the experience I had this morning was horrible. I stopped by the drive thru since l was on a tight schedule. With one person in front of me, it still took ten minutes to reach the window. I then was told the computer was down and being rebooted. Five minutes or so later, still nothing. Eventually another worker opens the window and says she's re-ringing the order but not charging me for the frozen mocha (I never ordered a frozen mocha). She finally found our sandwich, which I paid full price for. It was cold, hard, burnt, and made incorrectly... I didn't have time to complain since I was late and there were about 7 cars behind me by then. I'll never be going back to this location.

Great service! Kristen was so friendly and helpful. We had the beer tastings, usually we get the wine, thought we'd try something new. We were not disappointed. This is a great place with an awesome location and excellent service

Had a great experience. Place is really clean and has cool decor. Service was prompt and intuitive. The food was delicious. Make sure to leave room for dessert, the dessert menu is a picture book from their bakery. Prices were great as well!

Good buffet for the price. We went during the week and spent $27 for 2 people (11.99 each). They had everything you could ask for! Waiters grabbing drink orders. Eggs, bacon, sausage, cinnamon rolls, cereal, fruit, bagels, and much more! They also have a made to order station for eggs which was a plus because their buffet style eggs were a little too runny for my boyfriend. Overall, would definitely recommend for breakfast!

My favorite new delivery place!  They are always super nice, have great coupons, DELICIOUS crust and toppings and they're right next to Family Video - which rocks too!  Their garden salad could use some help but that's no biggie.  

Why someone complained about them on here without ever trying the food is stupid, call the manager - don't leave a 1star review because of a driver... 

Imos is ok for thin crust - but how do you compare them to this hand tossed pizza? It's like comparing apples and oranges.
Good price on labor i had a broken mudflap i had to get put back on for a good price

We, as a society, do not take enough time off.   That needs to change.   However, from time to time, you find a spot that allows you to feel like you are on a mini vacation.   Revolucion is that type of place.   Thanks to my fellow Yelpers, I had this on my "wish list" for a good while and on a "date night" with my better half, we received a "day pass" out of the suburbs for a night to visit Fountain Square.   
Walking in to the main bar area in the front, you get a sense that a great deal of time and effort was put into getting the decor just right.  
But then, the special treat.  Walking through what has a feel of a magical portal to vacation-land (for grownups), you enter the Tiki Bar area and instant relaxation.   I must say that the service was excellent and our bartender was fun and made us feel at home.   
The menu is straightforward, with a nice variety of appetizers (pinchos), tacos and burgers.   No fuss, no muss.  Being on the veggie side of the street, I ordered and enjoyed the Taco de Papas - which is two tacos with roasted potatoes, poblanos, corn and queso fresco and crema.   Just right.   
We would highly recommend Revolucion for both the service and the food.   Another special gem in an outstanding neighborhood!

I took an 8 year old and a 14 year old for the lunch special pizza.  We have done this on several occasions, and the kids love that they each get their own personal pizza, made the way they like.   They both ordered their pizza with 2 items and wanted BBQ sauce as the base instead of tomato sauce.  (this is the only way they enjoy pizza).   I was told that they could only get tomato sauce, not BBQ sauce.   I explained that we have gotten it this way several times before.   We were told that they don't offer it this way any more.   I see that some of the pizzas offer BBQ sauce and pointed it out, but again was told that it couldn't be made this way for them.   I asked if I could pay additional to have it made with BBQ sauce, but once again told it was not possible.   Sadly, we left the restaurant and chose a different nearby restaurant for lunch.  I'm sorry to say I won't be able to take the kids here anymore.
By far the best Jamaican food I've ever had. Costs a little more than others in the area but worth every extra penny. I had oxtail, Mac and cheese, and rice and beans and everything was delicious!

We tried this place because it was new to the area and we like to give new businesses a chance. When we walked in, the hostess seemed very a bit aloof to what was going on. After being sent to our table by the window, we ordered our food. My son ordered a chocolate chip pancake (with the chips just thrown on top and not even added to the batter) and my wife ordered a fish sandwich that looked like it was straight out of a bag from target. Then my we ordered a kids meal for my toddler and the nuggets were the same ones that you buy from the supermarket. Not only was the food store bought, we all got sick after our meal!! Not even an hour after we left my son and wife were running to the restroom. Extremely disappointed and disgusted with this place. I never enjoy giving negative reviews, but this needed to happen. STAY AWAY AT ALL COSTS!!

Coming from SoCal, we have been looking for an authentic taco experience. We stumbled upon this hidden gem recently and it did not disappoint.  Great, flavorful carne asada, tasty salsas and real horchata! Even the tortillas are made fresh! Stop by!

Ordered 4 pot pies she said they have them made. Then manager takes one and says I have to wait 20 minutes for another one and I should order something else. Every time I come here there's a problem. Go somewhere else.  How is a 20 minute menu item that is all over TV even a fast food item?

I will concur with the other reviews regarding poor service. The lady who took our order was ok but the lady who made our burritos was extremely rude to my wife and also had soap suds all over her forearm and thankfully it didn't touch our burrito. This is the closest qdoba to our home but next time will go somewhere else
I think this is a great place for people who want "kind of Latin food." It's overpriced. It's pretentious. It's like that girl you met in college from the suburbs.

It's rare when both my wife and I can say we ate the best of something at a restaurant. For her it was the Shrimp and Grits and for me it was the Creme Brûlée. The grits were simply heaven. The crawfish crepes and the boulabase were also great choices. I got an Old Fashioned made with my bourbon of choice to accompany my meal, but I can see how wine could be paired with the food as well.

The three course meal is a reasonable price for such high quality.
